tables/Army/ArmyComposition.md.title: ArmyComposition - army group composition
tables/Army/ArmyComposition.md.summary: ArmyComposition.xml defines the mix of elite, regular and admin soldiers in an army group, its priority, and its starting and target population.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/AdminPercen.description: Share or weight of administration soldiers in this composition, in percent.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/AdminPercen.numericSemantics: higher = larger admin share; the loader clamps values below 0 to 0 and above 100 to 100.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/DesiredPopu.description: Target number of soldiers the composition tries to maintain.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/DesiredPopu.numericSemantics: higher = larger target; the loader clamps negative values to 1.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/DesiredPopu.values: 1..127 after clamping; the loader stores this field as INT8.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/ElitePercen.description: Share of elite soldiers in this composition, in percent.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/ElitePercen.numericSemantics: higher = larger share; the loader clamps values below 0 to 0 and above 100 to 100.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Index.description: Index of the army composition. It is an array key used by garrisons and patrols.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Index.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Index.source: game code (army composition loader); table data.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Priority.description: Priority of this composition relative to the others.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Priority.numericSemantics: higher = more important; negative values are not meaningful.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/Priority.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/StartPopula.description: Number of soldiers in the composition at campaign start.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/StartPopula.numericSemantics: higher = more soldiers; the loader clamps negative values to 1.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/StartPopula.values: 1..127 after clamping; the loader stores this field as INT8.

COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/TroopPercen.description: Share of regular troop soldiers in this composition, in percent.
COMPOSITION_INFO/COMPOSITION/TroopPercen.numericSemantics: higher = larger share; the loader clamps values below 0 to 0 and above 100 to 100.

tables/Army/PatrolGroups.md.title: PatrolGroups - army patrol routes
tables/Army/PatrolGroups.md.summary: PatrolGroups.xml defines army patrol groups by priority, size and up to four waypoint sectors. A patrol follows its listed waypoints in order; unused waypoints are left empty or set to 0.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Priority.description: Patrol priority: how important the patrol group is to the Queen.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Priority.numericSemantics: higher = more important; more important patrols get more reinforcement/upgrade chances. The XML comment gives the intended range 0..100.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Priority.values: 0..100; the loader stores this field as INT8.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Priority.source: game code (patrol loader); table XML comment.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Size.description: Base number of soldiers in the patrol. The actual group size is this value plus or minus one, then clamped to the INI group-size limits.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Size.numericSemantics: higher = larger patrol; the base value is varied by ±1 before clamping.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Size.values: Integer base size; the loader stores this field as INT8.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Size.source: game code (patrol loader); table XML comment.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector1.description: Patrol waypoint sector in A1..P16 form. The literal value 0 explicitly marks the waypoint as unused; an empty or malformed value is a parse error, not an unused waypoint.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector1.values: 0 or a sector such as A1, B5, P16.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector2.description: Patrol waypoint sector in A1..P16 form. The literal value 0 explicitly marks the waypoint as unused; an empty or malformed value is a parse error, not an unused waypoint.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector2.values: 0 or a sector such as A1, B5, P16.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector3.description: Patrol waypoint sector in A1..P16 form. The literal value 0 explicitly marks the waypoint as unused; an empty or malformed value is a parse error, not an unused waypoint.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector3.values: 0 or a sector such as A1, B5, P16.

PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector4.description: Patrol waypoint sector in A1..P16 form. The literal value 0 explicitly marks the waypoint as unused; an empty or malformed value is a parse error, not an unused waypoint.
PATROL_INFO/PATROL/Waypoints/Sector4.values: 0 or a sector such as A1, B5, P16.

tables/Army/UniformColors.md.title: UniformColors - enemy and militia uniform colours
tables/Army/UniformColors.md.summary: UniformColors.xml assigns a vest and pants colour to each enemy and militia rank. All six uniform blocks are mandatory; the loader throws an error if any is missing. Values must be one of the case-sensitive palette names listed in the XML comment, not arbitrary text.

UNIFORMS/ENEMY_ADMIN/Pants.values: Case-sensitive palette name from the XML comment: vest YELLOWVEST, BLACKSHIRT, REDVEST, GREENVEST, JEANVEST, BLUEVEST, greyVEST, GYELLOWSHIRT, WHITEVEST, PURPLESHIRT or BROWNVEST; pants GREENPANTS, BLACKPANTS, BEIGEPANTS, TANPANTS, JEANPANTS or BLUEPANTS. Free text is not valid.
UNIFORMS/ENEMY_ADMIN/Pants.default: Required; all six uniform blocks must define both Vest and Pants.

tables/Backgrounds.md.summary: Backgrounds.xml defines optional character backgrounds: skill and stat bonuses, assignment modifiers, environmental modifiers, resistances and background eligibility rules. The background system and IMP-creation options decide which rows are offered.

BACKGROUNDS/BACKGROUND/SAM_cth.numericSemantics: Signed background modifier: higher values mean a stronger positive bonus, and negative values mean a penalty.
BACKGROUNDS/BACKGROUND/SAM_cth.values: Integer modifier; no narrower range is declared by the field metadata.
BACKGROUNDS/BACKGROUND/SAM_cth.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`DifficultySettings.xml` defines the campaign difficulty levels: starting cash, enemy AP and group settings, queen economy, alert behavior, reinforcements, CTH constants and sector starting forces.

The loader keeps one working record for the whole file and copies it into the slot named by `uiIndex` when the record closes. An element omitted from a `DIFFICULTY` record therefore keeps the value from the previous record (or `0` for the first record), which also means `uiIndex` must be present in every record or that record overwrites the previous slot. All numeric elements are parsed with an integer parser, and only the low byte or word that the runtime field accepts survives, which makes some effective ranges much narrower than the signed business value suggests.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- This table is selected by the campaign difficulty setting; it does not reference item or profile rows.
- The `CthConstants*` fields are NCTH constants and are relevant only when NCTH is active.
- Difficulty level `0` is a placeholder; campaign setup uses levels `1..4`.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: `Name` and `ConfirmText` are display text; numeric settings are not localized.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Difficulty table data.
- Difficulty schema comments.
- Game code (difficulty loader, strategic AI, campaign initialisation, NCTH chance-to-hit, creature spreading and soldier creation).
- Field types are the types of the runtime `DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS_VALUES` fields and of the loader casts; descriptions follow the code that consumes each value.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `BloodcatAmbushSectors` is loaded into a boolean that no other code reads; the table comment only says `?`. Its intended behaviour is unknown.
- `CreaturePopulationModifier` is loaded and saved but not used by any population formula in this build; whether it was meant to feed the spreading chance is unknown.
- The seven `Sector*` fields are dead in this build: `BuildUndergroundSectorInfoList` always returns after the `initunderground.lua` path, so the hardcoded setup that reads them never runs. Whether that fallback was meant to remain reachable is unknown.
- The loader's read list uses `SectorK4B2NumElites`/`SectorO3B2NumElites` while the shipped data and the assignment cases use `SectorK4B1NumElites`/`SectorO3B1NumElites`; whether the names were meant to match is unknown.
- The exact interaction between difficulty levels and the hardcoded four-level logic is outside this table; the comment warns that new entries must not be created.

tables/Disease.md.title: Disease - disease definitions
tables/Disease.md.summary: Disease.xml defines each disease as a set of disease points plus the effects those points produce. Infection adds initial points; the points then rise or fall each hour until they cross the outbreak threshold, and the full threshold scales the symptoms. The table also defines the base chance for each infection source and the flags that control cure, reinfection, visibility and severe limitations. It is active only when the disease system is enabled.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Disease.xml` defines each disease as a set of disease points plus the effects those points produce. Infection adds initial points; the points then rise or fall each hour until they cross the outbreak threshold, and the full threshold scales the symptoms. The table also defines the base chance for each infection source and the flags that control cure, reinfection, visibility and severe limitations. It is active only when the disease system is enabled.

Infection chances are percentages, not points: each field is the base chance for one qualifying event, such as an hourly check in a swamp, a wound, or a bad meal. Disease resistance and situational modifiers reduce the final chance. Effects are defined at full infection and are interpolated from `1.0` down to the current magnitude.

sections.text: The table stores balance values; it does not define how often a sex encounter or a bad meal occurs. The exact splint and severe-limitation behavior is implemented by the disease code, not by additional XML fields.

ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/Sector.description: Sector code where the custom enemy group name applies. It is a map coordinate in A1..P16 form: one letter for the row and a decimal column number.
ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/Sector.numericSemantics: The loader accepts the first character as the row and the remaining digits as the column; it keeps the value only when both are in 1..16.
ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/Sector.values: A sector such as A1, B5 or P16; an out-of-range value leaves the previous/default coordinate unchanged.

ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/szGroup.description: Display name of the enemy group in that sector.

ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/uiIndex.description: Index of the enemy-name entry. It is an array key.
ENEMY_NAMES/NAME/uiIndex.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `bItemNoN` values reference [Items](../Items/Items.md) item indexes.
- The backup tables are aliases of the main gun-choice files; editing them does not change the live choice files.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: Display names and labels are localized through language overlays; numeric IDs and codes are not.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Table data.
- Field names, XML comments and observed values.
- Descriptions are inferred from names and observed values; no runtime formula is claimed.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text: - The backup files are documented as aliases. Confirm whether the game still loads any of them before treating them as live data.

tables/Items/Armours.md.title: Armours - body armour
tables/Items/Armours.md.summary: Armours.xml defines the protective values of body armour. An armour item in Items points to one row through its ubClassIndex; the row is stored in the runtime armour table. The values drive damage reduction, armour wear, Bobby Ray's filters and the item description panel.

ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubArmourClass.description: Body slot/class of the armour. It is not the protection value; it tells the UI and equipment checks whether this is a helmet, vest, leggings or plate.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubArmourClass.values: 0 helmet, 1 vest, 2 leggings, 3 plate, 4 monster, 5 vehicle.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubArmourClass.default: 0 (helmet) when the element is missing, because the record is zeroed first.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubArmourClass.source: game code (armour loader); related: Armour protection.

ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubCoverage.description: Percentage of the body slot covered by the armour. It is used as a multiplier in protection calculations and in the item comparison panel.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubCoverage.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more protection/coverage, and negative values are not meaningful.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubCoverage.values: percentage; stored as UINT8. No separate validation limit is documented.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubCoverage.default: 100 when ENABLE_ARMOR_COVERAGE is false. The option defaults to FALSE, so a default game forces every row to 100 and ignores the XML value. When coverage is enabled and the element is missing, the zeroed record yields 0.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubCoverage.source: game code (armour loader); related: Armour protection.

ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubDegradePercent.description: Percentage of the applied protection subtracted from the armour's status when it absorbs a hit.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubDegradePercent.numericSemantics: Percentage; higher values wear the armour out faster, 0 means no degradation, and negative values are not meaningful for this unsigned percentage.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubDegradePercent.values: percentage; stored as UINT8. No separate validation limit is documented.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubDegradePercent.source: game code (armour loader); related: Armour protection.

ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubProtection.type: Integer (UINT16 in the struct, cast to UINT8 by the loader)
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubProtection.description: Raw protection value of the armour. The loader casts the parsed value to UINT8, so values above 255 are truncated even though the struct field is UINT16.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubProtection.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more protection/coverage, and negative values are not meaningful.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubProtection.values: 0..255 effectively; the loader truncates to UINT8.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/ubProtection.source: game code (armour loader); related: Armour protection.

ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/uiIndex.description: Index of the row in the runtime armour table and the identity of the XML record. Items.ubClassIndex of an armour item points here.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/uiIndex.values: 0..N-1; non-negative array index. The loader ignores values outside the array.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/uiIndex.default: none; a missing value leaves the table slot at zero.
ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR/uiIndex.source: game code (armour loader); related: Armour protection.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Armours.xml` defines the protective values of body armour. An armour item in `Items`
points to one row through its `ubClassIndex`; the row is stored in the runtime armour table.
The values drive damage reduction, armour wear, Bobby Ray's filters and the item description
panel.

`Armours` is a flat table: one `ARMOUR` record per armour type, keyed by `uiIndex`.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Armours` | `Items/Armours.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same schema; values may differ |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
ARMOURLIST
└── ARMOUR
    ├── uiIndex
    ├── ubArmourClass
    ├── ubProtection
    ├── ubCoverage
    └── ubDegradePercent
```

The loader writes each record to `Armour[uiIndex]` when the `ARMOUR` element closes. A
duplicate `uiIndex` overwrites the earlier row. Records with an
`uiIndex` outside the array are ignored.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `Items.ubClassIndex` -> `Armours.uiIndex` for items whose `usItemClass` is
  `IC_ARMOUR`.
- `Armours.ubArmourClass` -> `ArmourClass` (`../Lookup.md#armourclass`).
- The item's `usItemClass` and `ubClassIndex` live in [Items](Items.md).

sections.heading: Related formulas
sections.text:
The multi-stage damage model has its own chapters in [Related formulas](../../FORMULAS.md):

- [Armour protection](../../FORMULAS.md#armour-protection) - coverage, condition, ammo
  penetration and wear.
- [Ammo and weapon damage dealt](../../FORMULAS.md#ammo-and-weapon-damage-dealt) - how the
  armour result becomes final damage.

The field entries above define the inputs; they do not repeat the formulas.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
No strings in this table. Armour names and descriptions are fields of `Items` and are
translated there.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
v4 and v5 use the same five fields and the same `ARMOURLIST/ARMOUR` structure. Values
may differ; compare the two files when a specific value matters. No overlay covers
`Items/Armours.xml`.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: the armour loader, the per-hit protection pass and the item setting that
  controls coverage.
- Table data: `Items/Armours.xml` values.
- The protection and wear calculation is described in
  [Related formulas](../../FORMULAS.md#armour-protection).

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The exact damage formula and how `ubProtection`, `ubCoverage` and ammo type combine are
  described in [Related formulas](../../FORMULAS.md); a full balance discussion is outside
  this table page.
- Duplicate `uiIndex` handling is "last record wins" in the loader; the consequence of a
  duplicate is the same as for any later row overwriting an earlier one.

sections.text: `AttachmentComboMerges.xml` defines a base item plus up to twenty attachments and the item produced when the complete combination is present. It is the attachment-combination counterpart of `Merges`.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
ATTACHMENTCOMBOMERGELIST
└── ATTACHMENTCOMBOMERGE
    ├── uiIndex
    ├── usItem
    ├── usAttachment1
    ├── usAttachment2
    ├── usAttachment3
    ├── usAttachment4
    ├── usAttachment5
    ├── usAttachment6
    ├── usAttachment7
    ├── usAttachment8
    ├── usAttachment9
    ├── usAttachment10
    ├── usAttachment11
    ├── usAttachment12
    ├── usAttachment13
    ├── usAttachment14
    ├── usAttachment15
    ├── usAttachment16
    ├── usAttachment17
    ├── usAttachment18
    ├── usAttachment19
    ├── usAttachment20
    └── usResult
```

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `usItem`, `usAttachment1..20` and `usResult` point to [Items](Items.md).
- Attachment order does not matter: every non-zero slot is searched by item ID, and the row matches when all of them are attached.
- Rows are evaluated in ascending index order and the first matching row wins; the scan stops at the first row whose `usItem` is `0`.
- The 20 attachment slots are filled in document order: the loader ignores the digit in the element name and does not bound-check the slot counter.
- `usResult` must be a legal item, otherwise the row is skipped.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: This table has no display strings; item names come from `Items`.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: `XML_ComboMergeInfo.cpp` (loader), `Items.cpp` (`GetAttachmentComboMerge` and `PerformAttachmentComboMerge`), `Item Types.h` (`ComboMergeInfoStruct`, `MAX_DEFAULT_ATTACHMENTS`).
- Attachment combo-merge table data.
- Item metadata.
- Field types and limits: `ComboMergeInfoStruct` members and the loader casts.
- Descriptions cover the code path that consumes each field; no row counts or observed data ranges are used.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text: The loader accepts any element whose name contains `usAttachment` and never counts them, so more than 20 attachment elements overflow the row structure; the table format does not express that case.

tables/Items/AttachmentInfo.md.summary: AttachmentInfo.xml adds attachment-specific metadata: which item class an attachment can attach to and which skill check (with modifier) is required.

ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.description: Skill check used when attaching the item. None disables the check.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.values: IDs from Lookup.SkillCheckType: 0 None, 1 Lockpick, 2 Elec. Lockpick, 3 Attach Timed Detonator, 4 Attach Remote Detonator, 5 Plant Timed Bomb, 6 Plant Remote Bomb, 7 Open With Crowbar, 8 Smash Door, 9 Disarm Trap, 10 Unjam Gun, 11 Notice Dart, 12 Lie to Queen, 13 Attach Special Item, 14 Attach Special Elec. Item, 15 Disarm Elec. Trap.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.source: attachment info table data; field metadata.

ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.description: Modifier added to the selected attachment skill check.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.numericSemantics: Signed modifier added directly to the skill value: positive values make the check easier, negative values make it harder.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.values: Integer modifier added to the selected skill check; the loader stores it as INT8.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/bAttac.source: game code (SkillCheck, iChance = iSkill + bChanceMod); attachment info table data.

ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiInde.description: Index of the attachment-information row and identity of the XML record.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiInde.values: Non-negative integer; unique within the file.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiInde.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiItem.description: Bitmask of item classes this attachment can attach to. The host item class must intersect this mask.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiItem.numericSemantics: Bitmask or enumerated code; individual bits/choices carry the meaning, so a larger number is not simply “more”. Negative values are not meaningful.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiItem.values: Bitmask of Lookup.ItemClass IDs. The attachment can be mounted on items whose class intersects this mask.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/uiItem.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/usItem.description: Item ID of the attachment described by this row.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/usItem.values: Item ID in Items; the item must be an attachment.
ATTACHMENTINFOLIST/ATTACHMENTINFO/usItem.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

tables/Items/AttachmentSlots.md.title: AttachmentSlots - NAS attachment slots
tables/Items/AttachmentSlots.md.summary: AttachmentSlots.xml defines the slots used by the New Attachment System: their names, accepted attachment classes, layout classes, panel positions and pocket mapping.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fBigSl.description: Marks the slot as a big slot; the item-description panel uses the big-slot graphic and the wide slot width for it.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fBigSl.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fBigSl.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; item-description slot layout); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fMulti.description: Marks the slot as one magazine or tube of a multi-shot launcher. When the slot list is built for a grenade or rocket launcher, each such slot consumes one unit of the weapon's magazine capacity, and slots are skipped once the capacity is exhausted.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fMulti.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/fMulti.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; NAS slot generation for multi-shot launchers); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasAtt.description: Bitmask of attachment classes that the slot accepts. The NAS slot search tests it with a bitwise AND against each attachment-class bit that the item accepts.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasAtt.numericSemantics: Bitmask; individual bits carry the meaning, so a larger number is not simply “more”. 0 means None.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasAtt.values: Bitmask of IDs from Lookup.NasAttachmentClass: 0 None, 1 Default, 2 Barrel, 4 Laser, 8 Sight, 16 Scope, 32 Stock, 64 Ammo, 128 Internal, 256 External, 512 Underbarrel, 1024 Grenade, 2048 Rocket, 4096 MOLLE Small, 8192 MOLLE Medium, 16384 Batteries. Combine bits with OR.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasAtt.default: 0 (None) when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasAtt.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; NAS slot selection); Lookup.NasAttachmentClass; attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasLay.description: Bitmask of layout classes to which the slot belongs. The NAS slot search tests it with a bitwise AND against the item's layout class. If the item has no slot for the specific layout, a slot with layout class 1 (Weapons) is used as the default fallback.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasLay.numericSemantics: Bitmask; individual bits carry the meaning, so a larger number is not simply “more”. 0 means None.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasLay.values: Bitmask of IDs from Lookup.NasLayoutClass: 0 None, 1 Weapons, 2 Multi-Shot Launchers, 4 Molle Leg Rigs, 8 Molle Vests, 16 Molle Combat Packs, 32 Molle Backpacks. Combine bits with OR.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasLay.default: 0 (None) when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/nasLay.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; NAS slot selection and default-layout fallback); Lookup.NasLayoutClass; attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/szSlot.description: Display name of the slot, used as the fast-help (tooltip) text for an empty attachment slot in the item description.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/szSlot.values: Free text, converted from UTF-8; stored in a 200-character buffer, and longer text is truncated.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/szSlot.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; item-description fast help); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/ubPock.description: For LBE items, the 1-based pocket index into the item's pocket-availability mask; the slot is offered only when that pocket is available. 0 means no pocket mapping, so the slot is not filtered by pocket availability.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/ubPock.numericSemantics: 0 = none; 1..N selects bit 1 << (value - 1) in the LBE pocket mask.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/ubPock.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8 (the usable range is the LBE pocket count).
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/ubPock.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/ubPock.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; NAS LBE slot filtering); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/uiSlot.description: Identity of the attachment slot. Rows are stored at this index, and the slot presentation and layout code refers to the slot by this value.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/uiSlot.numericSemantics: Array index. The loader parses the text with strtoul and stores the result in a UINT16 member; values outside the MAXITEMS bound are discarded, and duplicate indexes overwrite earlier rows. The slot search starts at 1 and stops at the first index whose uiSlotIndex is 0, so index 0 is not offered as a slot.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/uiSlot.values: 0..16000 (MAXITEMS bound); the loader stores this field as UINT16.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/uiSlot.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0, so the row is stored at index 0 and is not offered.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/uiSlot.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; NAS slot lookup); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.description: Horizontal offset in pixels of the slot icon, relative to the item-description panel origin. The icon is drawn at the panel X plus this value minus 6; a value above 300 suppresses drawing of the slot.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.numericSemantics: Pixel offset; larger values move right. Values 0..300 are drawn.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; item-description slot drawing); attachment slot table data.

ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.description: Vertical offset in pixels of the slot icon, relative to the item-description panel origin. The icon is drawn at the panel Y plus this value minus 1; a value above 300 suppresses drawing of the slot.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.numericSemantics: Pixel offset; larger values move down. Values 0..300 are drawn.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
ATTACHMENTSLOTLIST/ATTACHMENTSLOT/usDesc.source: game code (attachment-slot loader; item-description slot drawing); attachment slot table data.

```
    ├── fBigSlot
    └── ubPocketMapping
```

`uiSlotIndex` is the key: the loader stores each row at that array index. NAS slot lookups start
at index `1` and stop at the first index whose `uiSlotIndex` is `0`, so slot indexes must be
contiguous from `1` for later slots to be reachable.

tables/Items/Drugs.md.title: Drugs - drug effects
tables/Items/Drugs.md.summary: Drugs.xml defines drug effects: stat changes, disease changes, temporary disabilities and personality changes. A drug can contain several effect blocks of the same or different types.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/chance.description: Chance that this disability is applied. 0 and 100 both mean the effect always applies; values 1..99 are a percentage.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/chance.numericSemantics: Higher values up to 99 mean a greater chance; 0 is the always-apply shortcut.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/chance.default: 100 when omitted; the loader initializes every effect block to 100.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/chance.source: game code (drug loader and chance check); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/disabil.description: Disability added for the duration of the effect. Only one disability is active at a time: a later different disability replaces the earlier one, while the same disability accumulates duration.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/disabil.values: Disability ID: 0 None, 1 Heat intolerant, 2 Nervous, 3 Claustrophobic, 4 Nonswimmer, 5 Fear of insects, 6 Forgetful, 7 Psycho, 8 Deaf, 9 Shortsighted, 10 Hemophiliac, 11 Afraid of heights, 12 Self-harm.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/disabil.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/disabil.source: game code (drug loader; disability enum and application); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/duratio.description: Duration of the disability in turns. The game scales it by the percentage of the item that was used.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/duratio.numericSemantics: Time value; higher values mean a longer disability.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/duratio.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/duratio.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISABILITY_EFFECT/duratio.source: game code (drug loader; disability application and end-turn update); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/chance.description: Chance that this disease effect is applied. 0 and 100 both mean the effect always applies; values 1..99 are a percentage.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/chance.numericSemantics: Higher values up to 99 mean a greater chance; 0 is the always-apply shortcut.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/chance.default: 100 when omitted; the loader initializes every effect block to 100.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/chance.source: game code (drug loader and chance check); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/disease.description: Disease row affected by this drug. The value indexes the runtime disease table.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/disease.values: Disease row index in Disease; 0 is Arulcan plague, not an empty row.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/disease.default: 0 (Arulcan plague) when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/disease.source: game code (drug loader; disease-point application); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/size.description: Disease points added. The game multiplies the value by the used item percentage, then adds it; positive values increase the disease, negative values cure it, and the result is clamped by the disease's outbreak and full-infection thresholds.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/size.numericSemantics: Signed points; higher positive values advance the disease faster, and negative values reduce it.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/size.values: -2147483648..2147483647; the loader stores this field as INT32.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/size.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DISEASE_EFFECT/size.source: game code (drug loader; AddDiseasePoints); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/chance.description: Chance that this effect is applied when the drug is consumed. 0 and 100 both mean the effect always applies; values 1..99 are a percentage.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/chance.numericSemantics: Higher values up to 99 mean a greater chance; 0 is the always-apply shortcut.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/chance.default: 100 when omitted; the loader initializes every effect block to 100.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/chance.source: game code (drug loader and chance check); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/duration.description: Duration of the effect in turns. The game decrements it during the end-turn drug update.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/duration.numericSemantics: Time value; higher values mean a longer-lasting effect.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/duration.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/duration.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/duration.source: game code (drug loader; end-turn drug update); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/effect.description: Stat or resource changed by this effect.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/effect.values: IDs from the drug-effect enum: 0 HP, 1 BP, 2 AP, 3 Morale, 4 Physical resistance, 5 Strength, 6 Agility, 7 Dexterity, 8 Wisdom.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/effect.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/effect.source: game code (drug loader; DRUG_EFFECT_ enum); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/size.description: Strength of the effect. Positive values raise the affected stat or resource, negative values lower it.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/size.numericSemantics: Signed strength; for a newly applied effect the game multiplies it by the used item percentage before storing it. Shipped data uses negative values for effects such as alcohol's Wisdom penalty.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/size.values: -32768..32767; the loader stores this field as INT16.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/size.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/DRUG_EFFECT/size.source: game code (drug loader; effect application); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/chance.description: Chance that this personality effect is applied. 0 and 100 both mean the effect always applies; values 1..99 are a percentage.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/chance.numericSemantics: Higher values up to 99 mean a greater chance; 0 is the always-apply shortcut.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/chance.default: 100 when omitted; the loader initializes every effect block to 100.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/chance.source: game code (drug loader and chance check); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/durati.description: Duration of the personality effect in turns. The game scales it by the percentage of the item that was used.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/durati.numericSemantics: Time value; higher values mean a longer personality change.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/durati.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/durati.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/durati.source: game code (drug loader; personality application and end-turn update); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/person.description: Personality trait added for the duration of the effect. Only one personality is active at a time: a later different trait replaces the earlier one, while the same trait accumulates duration.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/person.values: Personality trait ID: 0 Normal, 1 Sociable, 2 Loner, 3 Optimist, 4 Assertive, 5 Intellectual, 6 Primitive, 7 Aggressive, 8 Phlegmatic, 9 Dauntless, 10 Pacifist, 11 Malicious, 12 Show-off. The engine enum also defines 13 Coward, although the table comment stops at 12.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/person.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/PERSONALITY_EFFECT/person.source: game code (drug loader; character-trait enum and application); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/opinionevent.description: If set and dynamic opinions are enabled, consuming the drug triggers the addiction opinion event, which other mercenaries judge negatively. The event fires only when at least one DRUG_EFFECT block was applied.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/opinionevent.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/opinionevent.source: game code (drug loader; drug application and dynamic-opinion code); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/szName.description: Name copied into DRUG.szName. The loader's comment calls it informational, and no display or gameplay code reads it; the item row carries the player-visible name.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/szName.values: Free text, truncated to the 80-character CHAR16 buffer.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/szName.source: game code (drug loader and DRUG struct); drug table data.

DRUGSLIST/DRUG/uiIndex.description: Index of the drug row and identity of the XML record. It is referenced by the item's drug-type field in Items.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/uiIndex.values: 0..99; the runtime NewDrug array has NEW_DRUGS_MAX (100) slots. The loader stores this field as UINT8 and does not range-check it before writing.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/uiIndex.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
DRUGSLIST/DRUG/uiIndex.source: game code (drug loader and NewDrug array); drug table data.

sections.text:
Repeated `DRUG_EFFECT` blocks of the same type are merged in code rather than replaced: the durations are averaged and the resulting size is recomputed from the combined effect total. The XML comment does not describe that merge, and the table cannot express the merge weights directly.

The editor metadata maps `Items.DrugType` to `Lookup.DrugType`, whose IDs are bit flags, but the game uses the item value as a direct index into `NewDrug`; shipped item values are sequential indices. The table records the code behaviour and does not resolve that metadata mismatch.

tables/Items/Explosives.md.summary: Explosives.xml defines the blast produced by explosive items, grenades, launcher warheads and environmental explosions. An explosive item points here through ubClassIndex; the row controls damage, radius, stun, fragments, gas/smoke duration and the animation used.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/bIndoorModifier.description: Multiplier applied to damage and stun when the explosion occurs indoors. 0 leaves the blast unchanged; 0.25 adds 25%, and -1 makes the indoor damage zero.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/bIndoorModifier.numericSemantics: Positive values increase the indoor blast, negative values reduce it, and 0 is neutral. The modifier is applied only when InARoom is true.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/bIndoorModifier.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/bIndoorModifier.source: game code (explosive loader; InARoom damage adjustment); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/fExplodeOnImpact.description: If set, an IC_EXPLOSV item detonates on impact instead of waiting for a fuse or remote trigger. Items of class IC_BOMB always detonate on impact regardless of this flag.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/fExplodeOnImpact.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/fExplodeOnImpact.source: game code (explosive loader; OBJECT_DETONATE_ON_IMPACT); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubAnimationID.description: Index of the blast animation and sound row in ExplosionData. It becomes the explosion's ubTypeID and selects the blast STI, frame counts and sound IDs.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubAnimationID.values: Index of a row in ExplosionData; shipped values are 0..15.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubAnimationID.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubAnimationID.source: game code (explosive loader; GenerateExplosion and ExplosionData lookup); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDamage.description: Base wound damage applied by the explosion. The game adds a random 0..99% roll and reduces the result by distance within ubRadius; when the explosion is indoors, bIndoorModifier is applied first.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDamage.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more damage; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDamage.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDamage.source: game code (explosive loader; explosion damage calculation); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDuration.description: Duration of a lingering effect. It is reused as the smoke/gas duration (in turns), the light-effect duration, the flashbang blind counter and the signal-shell wave count; 0 means no lingering effect.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDuration.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a longer-lasting effect, but the unit depends on the explosion type that consumes it.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDuration.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubDuration.source: game code (explosive loader; smoke, light and blinding code); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragDamage.description: Impact/damage value used for each fragment projectile.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragDamage.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more damage per fragment; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragDamage.values: 0..250; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragDamage.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragDamage.source: game code (explosive loader; fragment bullet impact); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragRange.description: Maximum travel range of fragments, in tenths of a tile (10 units = one tile). The game uses it as the fragment bullet's range.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragRange.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a longer fragment range; the display divides the value by CELL_X_SIZE (10) to show tiles.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragRange.values: 0..250; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragRange.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragRange.source: game code (explosive loader; FireFragments and fragment range display); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragType.description: Ammo type used for the fragment projectiles; it supplies the fragment's damage and impact behaviour.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragType.values: Index of a row in AmmoTypes; the fragment projectile uses that ammo type.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragType.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubFragType.source: game code (explosive loader; fragment bullet setup); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubHorizontalDegr.description: Full horizontal arc width of the fragment cone, in degrees, for directional explosives. Non-directional explosives ignore it and spread fragments randomly. The code takes the value modulo 360, so 360 behaves like 0 and 359 gives an almost full circle.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubHorizontalDegr.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a wider horizontal spread; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubHorizontalDegr.values: 0..360; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubHorizontalDegr.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubHorizontalDegr.source: game code (explosive loader; directional fragment spread); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubMagSize.description: Number of charges an explosive item contributes when loaded into a multi-shot grenade launcher. Values above 1 let the launcher fire the item repeatedly, and each shot reduces the item's status by ceil(100 / ubMagSize). It is not the blast radius.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubMagSize.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more shots per loaded item.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubMagSize.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubMagSize.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubMagSize.source: game code (explosive loader; GetExpMagSize and launcher ammo deduction); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubRadius.description: Effect radius in tiles. Damage falls off linearly with distance up to this radius; at or beyond it the damage becomes sWoundAmt / ubRadius / 2. 0 leaves the damage unreduced.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubRadius.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a wider blast; the loader clamps the parsed value to 0..255.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubRadius.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubRadius.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubRadius.source: game code (explosive loader; distance falloff); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStartRadius.description: Initial radius of the effect at the moment of detonation. Smoke and light start at this radius and the smoke effect expands toward ubRadius.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStartRadius.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger initial area; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStartRadius.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStartRadius.source: game code (explosive loader; smoke and light effect setup); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStunDamage.description: Base stun (breath) damage applied by the explosion. The same random roll (applied at half strength) and radius falloff as ubDamage apply, and bIndoorModifier is applied indoors.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStunDamage.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more stun/breath damage; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStunDamage.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubStunDamage.source: game code (explosive loader; explosion breath-damage calculation); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubType.description: Explosion type from Lookup.ExplosionType; it selects damage handling, gas/smoke behaviour and visual/sound treatment. The engine enum names for the last entries are EXPLOSV_BURNABLEGAS (8), EXPLOSV_SIGNAL_SMOKE (10), EXPLOSV_SMOKE_DEBRIS (11) and EXPLOSV_SMOKE_FIRERETARDANT (12).
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubType.values: IDs from Lookup.ExplosionType: 0 Normal, 1 Stun, 2 Tear Gas, 3 Mustard Gas, 4 Flare, 5 Noise, 6 Smoke, 7 Creature Gas, 8 Fire, 9 Flashbang, 10 Signal Shell, 11 Roof Collapse, 12 White Smoke.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubType.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubType.source: game code (explosive loader; EXPLOSV_ enum); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVerticalDegree.description: Full vertical arc width of the fragment cone, in degrees, for directional explosives. Non-directional explosives ignore it and spread fragments randomly. The code takes the value modulo 180, so 180 behaves like 0.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVerticalDegree.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a wider vertical spread; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVerticalDegree.values: 0..360 in the metadata; the code uses the value modulo 180.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVerticalDegree.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVerticalDegree.source: game code (explosive loader; directional fragment spread); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolatility.description: Base volatility used by the chain-reaction check when the explosive item takes damage. It is not a direct percentage: the game converts it to 50 + (value - 1) 10 on the ground or 3 + (value - 1) 3 when carried, then scales that by the item's condition and the damage taken.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolatility.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a more volatile explosive; 0 disables accidental detonation.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolatility.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolatility.source: game code (explosive loader; CheckForChainReaction and CalcTotalVolatility); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolume.description: Noise volume of the explosion passed to MakeNoise with NOISE_EXPLOSION. It affects AI hearing and is not the sound-playback volume.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolume.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a louder explosion; 0 makes it silent to the noise system.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolume.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolume.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/ubVolume.source: game code (explosive loader; explosion noise); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/uiIndex.description: Index of the explosion row in the runtime explosion table. Items.ubClassIndex of an explosive item points here.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/uiIndex.values: 0..16000; the loader writes into Explosive[MAXITEMS] with MAXITEMS = 16001, and rows with a larger uiIndex are silently ignored.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/uiIndex.default: missing or empty means 0; the parser zeroes the record, so such a row is stored at index 0.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/uiIndex.source: game code (explosive loader and runtime Explosive array); explosive table data.

EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/usNumFragments.description: Number of fragment projectiles produced by the explosion. Fragments spawn whenever this value is positive, except in water and in multiplayer; the AI damage estimate adds fragment damage only for EXPLOSV_NORMAL explosions.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/usNumFragments.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more fragments; each fragment uses ubFragType, ubFragDamage and ubFragRange.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/usNumFragments.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
EXPLOSIVELIST/EXPLOSIVE/usNumFragments.source: game code (explosive loader; FireFragments and fragment damage); explosive table data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `Explosives.xml` defines the blast produced by explosive items, grenades, launcher warheads and environmental explosions. An explosive item points here through `ubClassIndex`; the row controls damage, radius, stun, fragments, gas/smoke duration and the animation used.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Explosives` | `Items/Explosives.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same 19 field paths, including `bIndoorModifier`; the reference files contain the same values. |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
EXPLOSIVELIST
└── EXPLOSIVE
    ├── uiIndex
    ├── ubType
    ├── ubDamage
    ├── ubStunDamage
    ├── ubRadius
    ├── ubVolume
    ├── ubVolatility
    ├── ubAnimationID
    ├── ubDuration
    ├── ubStartRadius
    ├── ubMagSize
    ├── fExplodeOnImpact
    ├── usNumFragments
    ├── ubFragType
    ├── ubFragDamage
    ├── ubFragRange
    ├── ubHorizontalDegree
    ├── ubVerticalDegree
    └── bIndoorModifier
```

sections.heading: Game options
sections.text: No table-level global option is documented for this table. The records are independent of the inventory model. Fragment spawning is disabled in multiplayer (`FireFragments` returns immediately when networked); the other fields are used normally.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `Items.ubClassIndex` of an explosive item points to `Explosives.uiIndex`.
- `ubAnimationID` points to [ExplosionData](ExplosionData.md).
- `ubFragType` points to [AmmoTypes](AmmoTypes.md) for fragment behaviour.
- `ubType` uses [Lookup.ExplosionType](../Lookup.md#explosiontype).

sections.heading: Related formulas
sections.text: No formula in [FORMULAS](../../FORMULAS.md) applies to this table.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: This table has no display strings; localized names and descriptions live on the item row in `Items`.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same 19 field paths, and `bIndoorModifier` is present in both. The reference v4 and v5 files contain identical values.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Explosive table data.
- Game code (explosive loader, explosion table struct, explosion, fragment and chain-reaction functions).
- Item metadata and lookup tables.
- Field types and limits: item metadata; numeric limits use the metadata validation ranges.
- Semantic descriptions use the game code; entries marked `inferred` do not claim a code-verified formula.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text: `ubDuration` is a single value reused for smoke duration, light-effect duration, the flashbang blind counter and signal-shell waves. The table cannot express different durations for those effects; the unit and meaning depend on the explosion type that consumes it.

tables/Items/Food.md.title: Food - food and drink values
tables/Items/Food.md.summary: Food.xml defines the food and drink values of consumable items: food points, drink points, morale modifier and decay rate.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/bDrinkPoints.description: Drink points supplied when the item is consumed.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bDrinkPoints.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger quantity; negative values are not meaningful.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bDrinkPoints.values: Drink points supplied by the item; no narrower range is declared by the field metadata.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bDrinkPoints.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bDrinkPoints.source: game code (food loader); food table data.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/bFoodPoints.description: Food points supplied when the item is consumed.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bFoodPoints.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger quantity; negative values are not meaningful.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bFoodPoints.values: Food points supplied by the item; no narrower range is declared by the field metadata.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bFoodPoints.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bFoodPoints.source: game code (food loader); food table data.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/bMoraleMod.description: Legacy morale value present in Food.xml. The current food loader does not read this element; food morale is driven by the FoodMoraleMods thresholds instead.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bMoraleMod.numericSemantics: Signed legacy value; it has no effect through the current loader.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bMoraleMod.values: Integer; retained for compatibility with existing XML.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/bMoraleMod.source: game code (the food loader has no bMoraleMod case); food table data.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/szName.description: Informational label for the food or drink. The current food loader reads the element but does not use it for gameplay or display lookup.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/szName.source: game code (food loader ignores the value); food table data.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/uiIndex.description: Index of the food row and identity of the XML record.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/uiIndex.values: Non-negative index; unique within the file. It is referenced by the item row through the food type.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/uiIndex.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/uiIndex.source: game code (food loader); food table data.

FOODSLIST/FOOD/usDecayRate.description: Decay rate of the food item; the unit is defined by the food system.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/usDecayRate.numericSemantics: Higher values mean faster decay, and negative values are not meaningful.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/usDecayRate.values: Decimal decay rate; the unit is defined by the food system.
FOODSLIST/FOOD/usDecayRate.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

tables/Items/FoodOpinion.md.title: FoodOpinion - profile food preferences
tables/Items/FoodOpinion.md.summary: FoodOpinion.xml stores per-profile food preferences: each row links a profile to a food row and gives the morale modifier for that combination.

FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.description: Food row that the profile likes or dislikes.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.description: Morale modifier applied to this profile when it consumes the food.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.numericSemantics: Signed morale modifier: positive values improve morale, negative values reduce it, and 0 is neutral.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.values: Morale modifier for this profile and food.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/PROFILE_OPI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/uProfile.description: Profile whose food preference is described by this row.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/uProfile.values: Profile ID; the loader stores one entry per profile, so a later row for the same profile overwrites the earlier one.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/uProfile.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
FOODOPINIONSLIST/FOODOPINION/uProfile.source: game code (food-opinion loader); food opinion table data.

tables/Items/Item_Transformations.md.title: Item_Transformations - item transformations
tables/Items/Item_Transformations.md.summary: Item_Transformations.xml defines a transformation menu for an item: AP and breath-point (BP) costs, up to ten result items, and the menu/tooltip text shown to the player.

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/iBPCost.type: Integer (INT32) — it is not a UINT16.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/iBPCost.description: Breath-point cost of the transformation, not a blueprint or creation-point cost. A positive value is breath lost and a negative value is breath gained.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/iBPCost.numericSemantics: BP (breath). EnoughPoints checks only the AP part, so the breath change is applied by DeductPoints without a sufficiency test; robots and vehicles skip it.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/iBPCost.values: Breath points; positive = cost, negative = gain.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/iBPCost.source: game code (the transformation loader; the breath-point deduction, whose comment reads “iBPCost > 0 - breath loss, iBPCost < 0 - breath gain”).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szMenuRow.type: String — stored as a 50-character wide string.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szMenuRow.description: Label of the transformation menu row. The loader converts the UTF-8 text into a fixed CHAR16[50] buffer and forces the last position to '\0', so about 49 characters fit and longer text cannot be stored.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szMenuRow.values: Free text; a short action label rather than a full sentence.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szMenuRow.source: game code (the transformation loader; the transformation record).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szTooltip.type: String — stored as a 300-character wide string.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szTooltip.description: Tooltip shown for the transformation menu row, read into a fixed CHAR16[300] buffer.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/szTooltip.source: game code (the transformation loader; the transformation record).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usAPCost.description: Action-point cost of the transformation. The loader rescales the value with DynamicAdjustAPConstants, i.e. value AP_MAXIMUM / 100 rounded, so the cost follows the AP system in the AP/BP constants file; AP_MAXIMUM defaults to 100, which leaves the value unchanged.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usAPCost.numericSemantics: AP. It is charged only in turn-based combat — in real time the AP part is zeroed — and the menu appends (N AP) to the row when the cost is above 0 and combat is turn-based.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usAPCost.values: AP; 0 makes the transformation free in action points.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usAPCost.source: game code (the transformation loader; the AP-constant adjustment; the point checks; the menu).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usItem.description: Item ID of the item being transformed. The record itself is stored at Transform[N] where N is the row's document position, not at usItem, so this field only links the row to its item. Several rows may name the same item, and each matching row becomes one entry in the menu. Rows past MAXITEMS are dropped.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usItem.numericSemantics: Parsed through an INT16, so a literal above 32767 arrives negative and is then stored unchanged in a UINT16. A missing element leaves the pre-set -1 (65535), which is the sentinel that stops every menu and lookup scan — a row without usItem therefore hides the rest of the table.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usItem.values: Item ID; 0 and negative values also trip a debug assertion (Entry #N missing proper <usItem> tag).
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usItem.default: 65535 (0xFFFF) when omitted, which is not the same as 0.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usItem.source: game code (the transformation loader; the menu and lookup stop at 65535).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usResult1.description: Item ID produced in the first result slot. Slots are filled in document order: the loader accepts any element name containing usResult and writes each value into the next slot, so the trailing digit is ignored and a usResult2 placed before usResult1 would land in slot 1. 0 leaves the slot empty; the same item may appear in several slots.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usResult1.numericSemantics: Only slots above 0 produce items, and a positive value that names a random-item entry is resolved to a concrete item first.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usResult1.values: Item ID; 0 leaves the slot empty. The game reads exactly 10 slots (MAX_NUM_TRANSFORMATION_RESULTS), while the loader does not bound its counter, so an eleventh usResult element would be written past the array.
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usResult1.source: game code (the transformation loader; TransformObject; 10 result slots).

TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST/TRANSFORM/usResult1.description: Item ID produced in result slot 10, the last of the ten slots. Like every usResult element it is placed by document order, not by its digit. Zero leaves the slot empty; the same item may appear in several slots.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `Item_Transformations.xml` defines a transformation menu for an item: AP and breath-point (BP) costs, up to ten result items, and the menu/tooltip text shown to the player.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Item_Transformations` | `Items/Item_Transformations.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same field paths; values differ. |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
TRANSFORMATIONS_LIST
└── TRANSFORM
    ├── usItem
    ├── usResult1
    ├── usResult2
    ├── usResult3
    ├── usResult4
    ├── usResult5
    ├── usResult6
    ├── usResult7
    ├── usResult8
    ├── usResult9
    ├── usResult10
    ├── usAPCost
    ├── iBPCost
    ├── szMenuRowText
    └── szTooltipText
```

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `usItem` and `usResult1..10` point to [Items](Items.md).
- A row is found by scanning the loaded `Transform` array for a matching `usItem`; the first row whose `usItem` is `65535` stops the scan, and every matching row becomes an entry in the menu.
- The menu and tooltip strings are presentation data; the action itself is defined by the costs and results.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: `szMenuRowText` and `szTooltipText` are player-facing text and may be localized by the item overlay.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Item transformation table data.
- Game code: the transformation loader, the transformation record structure, the item transformation routine, the transformation menu and lookup, and the AP/BP handling.
- Field types are the storage types of the game structure; the editor's generic `Integer` kind does not distinguish the unsigned widths used above.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- No open question remains for `iBPCost`: it is the breath-point cost, positive for breath lost and negative for breath gained.
- No open question remains for the menu order: entries follow the document order of the `<TRANSFORM>` rows, and each row matching the item ID becomes one entry.
- Not established here: whether any tool validates `usAPCost` against the `AP_MAXIMUM` rescale; the table always stores the pre-scale value.

Each ITEM record defines one item ID, its name and description, its class, inventory data, combat modifiers, flags and links to class-specific tables. Other tables use the item uiIndex as a foreign key, so this table is the hub of most item relationships.
