ITEMLIST/ITEM/nasLayoutClass.description: NAS layout-class bit mask. It tells the NAS layout which attachment slots the item exposes; bits are defined by NasLayoutClass.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/nasLayoutClass.numericSemantics: Bitmask or enumerated code; individual bits/choices carry the meaning, so a larger number is not simply “more”. Negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/nasLayoutClass.values: 0 = none; parsed with atof and truncated to UINT64, so only decimal text is read; stored as UINT64.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/nasLayoutClass.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/nasLayoutClass.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatCooldownModificato.description: Percentage modifier of the cooldown amount; applies to guns and barrels.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatCooldownModificato.numericSemantics: Signed modifier: higher values mean a stronger positive effect, and negative values apply the opposite effect.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatCooldownModificato.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatCooldownModificato.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatDamageThresholdMod.description: Percentage modifier of the gun's damage threshold.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatDamageThresholdMod.numericSemantics: Signed modifier: higher values mean a stronger positive effect, and negative values apply the opposite effect.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatDamageThresholdMod.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatDamageThresholdMod.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatJamThresholdModifi.description: Percentage modifier of the gun's jam threshold.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatJamThresholdModifi.numericSemantics: Signed modifier: higher values mean a stronger positive effect, and negative values apply the opposite effect.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatJamThresholdModifi.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatJamThresholdModifi.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatTemperatureModific.description: Percentage modifier of the heat a shot generates (normally read from attachments).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatTemperatureModific.numericSemantics: Signed modifier: higher values mean a stronger positive effect, and negative values apply the opposite effect.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatTemperatureModific.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/overheatTemperatureModific.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitem.description: Random-item table ID used when this item is generated as random loot.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitem.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitem.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitemcoolnessmodifica.description: Coolness adjustment applied when this item is chosen as random loot.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitemcoolnessmodifica.numericSemantics: Signed coolness adjustment, clamped by the loader to -20..20.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitemcoolnessmodifica.values: -20..20; the loader clamps the value to this range; stored as INT8.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitemcoolnessmodifica.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/randomitemcoolnessmodifica.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/sBackpackWeightModifier.description: Carry-strength modifier applied when the item is in the backpack.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sBackpackWeightModifier.numericSemantics: Signed modifier; higher values mean a stronger positive effect, and negative values apply the opposite effect (a penalty or reduction).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sBackpackWeightModifier.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sBackpackWeightModifier.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/sFireResistance.numericSemantics: Signed resistance: higher values mean more fire resistance; the loader caps the value at 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sFireResistance.values: -32768..32767; the loader caps the value at 100 but does not clamp the lower bound; stored as INT16.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sFireResistance.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/sFireResistance.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/spreadPattern.description: Named shotgun pellet spread pattern from SpreadPatterns. The loader accepts either a pattern name or a numeric index; an unknown name or an out-of-range index resolves to 0, the default pattern.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/spreadPattern.numericSemantics: The stored value is the index of the pattern in SpreadPatterns.xml; 0 is the default pattern.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/spreadPattern.values: A pattern name from SpreadPatterns.xml or a numeric index into that table; empty, an unknown name or an out-of-range index resolves to 0 (default).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/spreadPattern.default: Empty; the loader resolves it to the default pattern 0.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/spreadPattern.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/szBRDesc.values: Up to 399 characters plus the terminator (CHAR16[400]); longer text is truncated by the loader.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szBRDesc.source: game code (item loader); item table data; item localization overlay.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szBRDesc.confidence: source Classification and attachment points. Item class, attachment systems and class dispatch.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/szBRName.values: Up to 79 characters plus the terminator (CHAR16[80]); longer text is truncated by the loader.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szBRName.source: game code (item loader); item table data; item localization overlay.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemDesc.description: Item description shown in the detail panel.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemDesc.values: Up to 399 characters plus the terminator (CHAR16[400]); longer text is truncated by the loader.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemDesc.source: game code (item loader); item table data; item localization overlay.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemName.description: Short item name used in lists and compact cells.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemName.values: Up to 79 characters plus the terminator (CHAR16[80]); longer text is truncated by the loader.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szItemName.source: game code (item loader); item table data; item localization overlay.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/szLongItemName.description: Full item name used in detail panels and tooltips.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szLongItemName.values: Up to 79 characters plus the terminator (CHAR16[80]); longer text is truncated by the loader.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/szLongItemName.source: game code (item loader); item table data; item localization overlay.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubClassIndex.description: Index of the class-specific record selected by usItemClass: an armour row, magazine row, weapon row, explosive row, and so on.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubClassIndex.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubClassIndex.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCoolness.description: Coolness/progress level at which the item becomes available in the campaign. The random-merc gear code skips items with ubCoolness < 1.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCoolness.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a later/rarer coolness tier; negative values are outside the normal range.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCoolness.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCoolness.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCursor.description: Cursor lookup ID shown when the item is selected in the inventory. See Cursor.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCursor.values: Lookup ID (0..255, stored as UINT8); see Cursor.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCursor.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubCursor.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicNum.description: Graphic index inside the library selected by ubGraphicType.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicNum.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicNum.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicType.description: Graphic library for the inventory picture: 0 gun/weapon graphics, 1 big-item graphics (P1ITEMS), 2 interface graphics (P2ITEMS), 3 alternate interface graphics (P3ITEMS), 4 and above further item tile libraries (P4ITEMS onward).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicType.values: 0..255; stored as UINT8. 0 selects the gun graphic libraries, 1..3 select P1ITEMS..P3ITEMS, and 4 and above select P4ITEMS and later item tile libraries.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicType.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubGraphicType.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubPerPocket.description: Old-inventory (OIV) pocket capacity: how many identical items fit into one pocket. Zero means no stacking. In NIV the field does not control pocket capacity (LBE/Pockets and ItemSize do), but the item-description code still reads it for the "small" property: under NIV every item otherwise reports as fitting a small pocket.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubPerPocket.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger pocket capacity, and negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubPerPocket.values: 0..255; stored as UINT8. The OIV slot capacity taken from it is clamped to MAX_OBJECTS_PER_SLOT (255).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubPerPocket.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubPerPocket.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubWeight.description: Item weight in the game's weight units; used by carry strength and backpack capacity. Two units are approximately one kilogram (roughly one unit per pound).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubWeight.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a heavier item; negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubWeight.values: 0..65535; stored as UINT16; the value is a whole number of weight units.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubWeight.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/ubWeight.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/uiIndex.description: Primary item ID. Cross-table references and localization overlays use this value; it is unique inside one file. A record whose usItemClass is 0 is skipped by the loader (only its text is copied in a localized overlay pass).
ITEMLIST/ITEM/uiIndex.values: 0..4294967295; stored as UINT32. The array has MAXITEMS (16001) entries; a larger index is ignored.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/uiIndex.default: None; required and unique inside the file.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/uiIndex.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usActionItemFlag.description: Bit mask of action-item flags. It controls special use actions such as NET, radio, or remote detonator.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usActionItemFlag.values: 0 = none; 0..4294967295; parsed with strtoul base 0 (hexadecimal 0x... is accepted); stored as UINT32.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usActionItemFlag.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usActionItemFlag.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usAdministrationModifier.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a stronger administration effect; 0 means no modifier, and negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usAdministrationModifier.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usAdministrationModifier.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usAdministrationModifier.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usBurialModifier.numericSemantics: Unsigned modifier; the loader keeps at most 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usBurialModifier.values: 0..100 effectively: the loader casts to UINT8 and keeps at most 100, so values above 100 and negative values both store as 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usBurialModifier.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usBurialModifier.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usHackingModifier.numericSemantics: Unsigned modifier; the loader keeps at most 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usHackingModifier.values: 0..100 effectively: the loader casts to UINT8 and keeps at most 100, so values above 100 and negative values both store as 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usHackingModifier.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usHackingModifier.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usItemClass.description: Bit mask of item-class flags (IC_). It selects the class-specific subtable reached through ubClassIndex and controls which item behaviours apply. A record with 0 is skipped by the loader. See Lookup.ItemClass.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usItemClass.numericSemantics: Bitmask or enumerated code; individual bits/choices carry the meaning, so a larger number is not simply “more”. Negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usItemClass.values: 0 = none; 0..4294967295; parsed with strtoul base 0 (hexadecimal 0x... is accepted); stored as UINT32.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usItemClass.default: None; every item declares a class.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usItemClass.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usOverheatingCooldownFacto.description: Temperature units removed per cooldown tick (roughly every turn or five seconds), before attachment and global modifiers.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usOverheatingCooldownFacto.numericSemantics: Higher values cool the weapon faster; 0 means no cooling, and negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usOverheatingCooldownFacto.default: 0 when omitted; the loader starts from zero. 100 is a data value, not a code default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usOverheatingCooldownFacto.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPortionSize.description: Portion size for food or drink items.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPortionSize.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger portion; negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPortionSize.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPortionSize.default: 100; the loader sets this before parsing the record.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPortionSize.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPrice.description: Base purchase price. Bobby Ray prices and some trade calculations derive from it.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPrice.numericSemantics: Amount of money or cost; higher values mean a larger amount, and negative values are not meaningful.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPrice.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usPrice.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldGraphic.description: Riot-shield graphic when the shield is deployed in tactical, taken from Tilecache/riotshield.sti.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldGraphic.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldGraphic.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldStrength.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a stronger shield; the loader caps the value at 100.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldStrength.values: 0..100; the loader caps the value at 100; stored as UINT16.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldStrength.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usRiotShieldStrength.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

ITEMLIST/ITEM/usSpotting.numericSemantics: Higher values improve spotting; 0 is neutral. The loader clamps the stored value to 0..100, so negative input becomes 0 rather than a penalty.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usSpotting.values: 0..100; the loader clamps the value to this range (min(100, max(0, ...))); stored as INT16.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usSpotting.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
ITEMLIST/ITEM/usSpotting.source: game code (item loader); item table data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Items.xml` is the master list of every item in the game. Each `ITEM` record
defines one item ID, its name and description, its class, inventory data,
combat modifiers, flags and links to class-specific tables. Other tables use
the item `uiIndex` as a foreign key, so this table is the hub of most item
relationships.

The table is flat: one `ITEM` record per item, keyed by `uiIndex`.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| File | Root / record | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Items/Items.xml` | `ITEMLIST` / `ITEM` | Base item table. |

The localized overlays (`Russian.Items.xml` and the other language files) are
not separate tables. They override the five text fields by `uiIndex`; see
[Localization](../../Localization.md).

- Root: `ITEMLIST`; record: `ITEM`; key: `uiIndex`.
- Flat fields plus three nested stance groups: `STAND_MODIFIERS`,
  `CROUCH_MODIFIERS` and `PRONE_MODIFIERS`. Each group holds eleven `INT16`
  modifiers. A missing crouch value inherits the standing value and a missing
  prone value inherits the crouch value; a missing standing value stays `0`.
- `DefaultAttachment` is a repeated element. A record may contain up to twenty
  occurrences (`MAX_DEFAULT_ATTACHMENTS`); each occurrence is one item ID.
  Values fill the first free slot, so a `0` entry is skipped and later values
  still load; occurrences beyond twenty are ignored. The documentation
  describes the path once and notes the repetition.
- Records are sparse in practice: missing fields take the game default, and
  empty elements are not the same as a numeric zero for text fields.
- Numeric fields keep their lexical form. A decimal such as `1.0` is not
  rewritten as `1` by the editor.

### Item classes and `ubClassIndex`

`usItemClass` is a bit mask. It selects the class-specific subtable used by
`ubClassIndex`:

- armour class -> [Armours](Armours.md);
- magazine/ammo class -> [Magazines](Magazines.md);
- launcher/ammo pairs -> [Launchables](Launchables.md);
- weapon, explosive and other class rows are documented in their own
  family documents.

Do not read `ubClassIndex` without `usItemClass`: the same number means a
different row in a different class table.

sections.heading: Game options
sections.text:
This table is shared by several optional systems. The option names below are
the ones that change how a field is read; a field without a note is used by
both variants of the relevant system. The general option map is
[OPTIONS.md](../../OPTIONS.md).

| Option | Values | Effect on this table |
|---|---|---|
| New Chance to Hit (NCTH) / old Chance to Hit (OCTH) | `NCTH = TRUE` or `FALSE` in the game option file. `TRUE` selects NCTH; `FALSE` selects OCTH. | NCTH reads `ScopeMagFactor`, `ProjectionFactor`, `RecoilModifierX`, `RecoilModifierY`, `PercentRecoilModifier`, `PercentAccuracyModifier` and the three stance groups. OCTH ignores those fields. |
| New inventory (NIV) / old inventory (OIV) | Selected when a new campaign starts; the choice is stored in the save. The 1.13 data set is NIV, and legacy OIV data remains supported. `OLD_INVENTORY_ITEM_NUMBER` (default `99`) marks the OIV-only item size. | `ubPerPocket` controls OIV pocket capacity only; in NIV the `Pockets` and `LoadBearingEquipment` tables and `ItemSize` control capacity. `NewInv` marks an item as NIV-only. In NIV, an item with `ItemSize` equal to `OLD_INVENTORY_ITEM_NUMBER` is excluded. |
| Sci-Fi mode | `SciFi = TRUE` or `FALSE`. | `SciFi` marks the item as part of the Sci-Fi item set. |
| Tons of Guns | `BigGunList = TRUE` or `FALSE`. | `BigGunList` includes the item in the expanded gun list. |
| Disease system | disease system enabled or disabled. | `DiseaseSystemExclusive` marks an item that belongs to the disease system. |

sections.heading: Field map
sections.text:
| Group | Fields | Covers |
|---|---:|---|
| Identity and descriptions | 6 | IDs, names and player-facing text. |
| Classification and attachment points | 10 | Item class, attachment systems and class dispatch. |
| Inventory, graphics and economy | 14 | Graphics, weight, size, price and Bobby Ray stock. |
| Food, drugs and action items | 6 | Consumable classes and special-use flags. |
| Weapon modifiers and overheating | 12 | Optics, recoil, accuracy, heat and dirt. |
| Robot, random loot and shield links | 7 | Robot damage, random-item links and riot-shield data. |
| Combat modifiers | 29 | To-hit, range, damage, AP, burst and autofire modifiers. |
| Camouflage, vision and body modifiers | 9 | Camo, stealth, spotting, vision and backpack/fire modifiers. |
| Attachment system, utility and transport | 23 | Attachment mode, kits, skills, transport progress and default attachments. |
| Item flags | 105 | Boolean item roles used across the game systems. |
| Stance modifier groups | 3 | Structural `STAND_MODIFIERS`, `CROUCH_MODIFIERS` and `PRONE_MODIFIERS` containers. |
| Stance modifier fields | 33 | Standing, crouching and prone aim modifiers. |

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `Items.uiIndex` is referenced by many tables: starting gear, random items,
  attachments, trader inventories, map extras and quest data.
- `Items.ubClassIndex` selects a row in the table chosen by `usItemClass`;
  see [Armours](Armours.md), [Magazines](Magazines.md) and
  [Launchables](Launchables.md).
- `Items.ubCursor` -> [Lookup.Cursor](../Lookup.md#cursor); `Items.Inseparable` -> [Lookup.Separability](../Lookup.md#separability).
- `Items.AttachmentClass` -> [Lookup.AttachmentClass](../Lookup.md#attachmentclass); `Items.nasAttachmentClass` ->
  [Lookup.NasAttachmentClass](../Lookup.md#nasattachmentclass); `Items.nasLayoutClass` -> [Lookup.NasLayoutClass](../Lookup.md#naslayoutclass).
- `Items.AttachmentPoint` and `Items.AvailableAttachmentPoint` ->
  [Lookup.AttachmentPoint](../Lookup.md#attachmentpoint); `Items.AttachmentSystem` -> [Lookup.AttachmentSystem](../Lookup.md#attachmentsystem).
- `Items.DrugType` -> [Lookup.DrugType](../Lookup.md#drugtype); `Items.FoodType` -> the [Food](Food.md) definitions.
- `Items.clothestype` -> the [Clothes](Clothes.md) definitions.
- `Items.spreadPattern` -> the [SpreadPatterns](../SpreadPatterns.md) definitions.
- `Items.DefaultAttachment`, `Items.DiscardedLauncherItem`,
  `Items.BloodiedItem`, `Items.buddyitem` and `Items.randomitem` are item or
  random-item IDs.
- `Items.usActionItemFlag` is a bit mask, not an item ID.

The translatable fields are `szItemName`, `szLongItemName`, `szItemDesc`,
`szBRName` and `szBRDesc`. They live in `Russian.Items.xml` and the other
language overlays, keyed by `uiIndex`. The base `Items.xml` remains the
schema and the fallback for untranslated fields. See

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
- v5 is the primary source for the document.
- v4 uses the same set of leaf paths; text and a few values differ because
  of localization and content edits.
- `DefaultAttachment` is one documented path with repeated elements; the
  repetition is a structural property, not a separate field.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Item table data: v5 primary, v4 comparison.
- Item property and flag metadata from the editor database.
- Lookup tables for cursors, attachment classes, separability, drugs and
  attachment systems.
- Localization overlays for the five text fields.
- Game C++ source: the `Items.xml` loader and the item struct in the item
  types header.

This block was checked against the game's `Items.xml` loader and the item
struct. The loader establishes the type, storage width, parse call and any
clamp or inheritance for every field; named bit meanings still come from the
lookup tables. The uncertainties that remain are listed below.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `DrugType`: the item struct defines the field as a flag mask; which bits map
  to which drug components still comes from the lookup.
- `FoodType`: the [Food](Food.md) table defines the rows; the item file stores
  only the class index.
- `bSoundType`: the full sound-family enum is not reconstructed.
- `RobotTargetingSkillGrant`, `RobotUtilitySkillGrant` and
  `RobotChassisSkillGrant`: the unit (skill points or skill level) is not
  verified.
- `TransportGroupMinProgress` and `TransportGroupMaxProgress`: the unit and scale
  are not confirmed; the document treats them as transport progress values.
- `BR_NewInventory`, `BR_UsedInventory` and `BR_ROF`: the loader keeps these in
  the Bobby Ray stock arrays, but the stock and restock formula is not
  reconstructed here.
- `RobotDamageReduction`: the loader only stores the decimal; whether the robot
  code treats it as a multiplier or a percentage is not reconstructed.
- `AttachmentClass`, `nasAttachmentClass` and `nasLayoutClass` are documented
  as bit masks; individual bit names live in the corresponding lookup pages.

tables/Items/Launchables.md.title: Launchables - launcher-to-ammo pairs
tables/Items/Launchables.md.summary: Launchables.xml lists which items a launcher can fire. Each record is a pair: the launcher item and the launchable ammo/projectile item. The game stores the pairs in Launchable[MAXITEMS+1][2] and uses them when a grenade launcher, rocket launcher or similar weapon selects ammunition.

LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/itemIndex.description: Item index of the launchable ammo/projectile in Items.uiIndex. It is the item the launcher fires.
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/itemIndex.values: valid Items.uiIndex values; stored as UINT16.
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/itemIndex.default: 0; a zero value is a data error.
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/itemIndex.source: game code (launcher loader); item table data.

LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/launchableInde.description: Item index of the launcher in Items.uiIndex. It identifies the weapon that can fire the item on the other side of the pair.
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/launchableInde.values: valid Items.uiIndex values; stored as UINT16.
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/launchableInde.default: 0; the pair is still stored, so a zero value is a data error, not "none".
LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE/launchableInde.source: game code (launcher loader); item table data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Launchables.xml` lists which items a launcher can fire. Each record is a pair: the launcher
item and the launchable ammo/projectile item. The game stores the pairs in
`Launchable[MAXITEMS+1][2]` and uses them when a grenade launcher, rocket launcher or similar
weapon selects ammunition.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Launchables` | `Items/Launchables.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same two fields |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
LAUNCHABLELIST
└── LAUNCHABLE
    ├── launchableIndex
    └── itemIndex
```

The loader does not use a key; it appends records in file order to the runtime pair table and
records the number of pairs. The editor uses the pair (`launchableIndex`, `itemIndex`) as a
compound key. Reordering records changes the runtime order, so treat the file order as
meaningful until a caller proves otherwise.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `Launchables.launchableIndex` -> [Items](Items.md) `uiIndex` (launcher).
- `Launchables.itemIndex` -> [Items](Items.md) `uiIndex` (ammo/projectile).
- The launcher item itself is an [Items](Items.md) record with a launcher class; the ammo item is
  usually an `IC_AMMO` or explosive item.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: No strings; both fields are numeric item indexes.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
v4 and v5 use the same `LAUNCHABLELIST/LAUNCHABLE` structure and the same two fields. Values
may differ; compare the files when a specific pair matters.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: the launcher/ammo pair loader.
- Table data: `Items/Launchables.xml`.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The loader appends in file order and does not deduplicate. The file has no duplicate
  pairs, but the runtime consequence of a duplicate is not documented.
- Which launcher classes use the table at runtime is decided in the item and weapon code;
  this page documents the data contract, not every call site.

tables/Items/LoadBearingEquipment.md.title: LoadBearingEquipment - NIV LBE layouts
tables/Items/LoadBearingEquipment.md.summary: LoadBearingEquipment.xml defines the pocket layout of LBE items in the New Inventory System: class, volume, available pocket bitmask and the pocket row assigned to each slot.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Volume capacity of the LBE. Contents are rejected when the volume already taken plus the volume of the pocket being filled exceeds this value, and the item description shows the used/available volume.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.numericSemantics: Volume units; 0 means the item is not a volume-limited carrier (the shipped table leaves most rows at 0 and uses 12..100 for the carriers).
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the volume check; the item-description line).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.type: Integer (UINT32) — the game stores this field in a UINT32.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: LBE class. Together with the item class it decides which body slot the piece occupies (thigh, vest, combat pack, backpack).
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: The game enum eLBE_CLASS is 1 THIGH_PACK, 2 VEST_PACK, 3 COMBAT_PACK, 4 BACKPACK, 5 LBE_POCKET, 6 OTHER_POCKET. Lookup.LBEClass names 0 Nothing through 4 Backpack; the shipped table only uses 1..4, and 0 is not a class the slot checks recognise.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the LBE class enum; per-slot class checks); Lookup.LBEClass.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.type: Integer (UINT32) — parsed with a base-0 conversion, so decimal or 0x hex.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Compatibility bitmask for LBE pieces worn at the same time (for example a combat pack over a backpack). Two pieces may be worn together only when their masks share at least one bit, and the piece already worn must itself have a non-zero mask.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.numericSemantics: Bitmask; combine bits with OR. A larger value is not “more” of anything. 0 shares no bit with anything, so it cannot be combined.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Up to 32 bits; the shipped table uses 0..4 and most rows are 0.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the lbeCombo field comment “Increased the LBE combo to 32bit … bitwise system”; combat-pack/backpack checks).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.type: Integer (UINT8) — the game stores this field in a UINT8, so values above 255 truncate.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Item size the LBE counts as when its pockets are full. CalculateItemSize starts from Item[usItem].ItemSize, adds the share of lbeFilledSize - ItemSize that matches how much of the pockets is used, and never exceeds max(ItemSize, lbeFilledSize).
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.numericSemantics: An item-size value, not a quantity; the shipped rows use 0, 10 and 22..34, which are item sizes.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the LBE loader; the item-size calculation).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Ordinal of the LBE row. The loader appends each record to the game's LoadBearingEquipment list in document order and stores this value without using it for placement, so it has to match the row's 0-based position; the game itself never reads the stored value.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: 0..65535; write the rows in ascending order. Items.ubClassIndex selects a row by its position in that list, and the debug writer re-emits the loop counter as lbeIndex.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the LBE loader; the item lookup uses the row position, not this value).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.type: Integer (UINT8) — the game stores each pocket index in a UINT8, so values above 255 truncate.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 1. The loader accepts lbePocketIndex1 and the dotted spelling lbePocketIndex.1 and writes the value into the first pocket slot.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; the game allocates 12 pocket slots and zero-fills them.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the LBE loader; 12 pocket slots).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 10 (lbePocketIndex10 or lbePocketIndex.10). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 11 (lbePocketIndex11 or lbePocketIndex.11). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 12, the last of the 12 slots (lbePocketIndex12 or lbePocketIndex.12). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the LBE loader; 12 pocket slots).

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 2 (lbePocketIndex2 or lbePocketIndex.2). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 3 (lbePocketIndex3 or lbePocketIndex.3). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 4 (lbePocketIndex4 or lbePocketIndex.4). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 5 (lbePocketIndex5 or lbePocketIndex.5). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 6 (lbePocketIndex6 or lbePocketIndex.6). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 7 (lbePocketIndex7 or lbePocketIndex.7). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 8 (lbePocketIndex8 or lbePocketIndex.8). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Pocket row assigned to slot 9 (lbePocketIndex9 or lbePocketIndex.9). 0 leaves the slot inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: Pocket row index in Pockets; 0 leaves the slot inactive.

LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.description: Bitmask of pocket slots whose pocket is supplied by an LBE attachment worn on the item (MOLLE). When lbePocketIndex for a slot is 0 and the matching bit is set, the game looks for an attachment in the attachment slot whose ubPocketMapping - 1 equals that pocket number and uses the attachment's first non-zero pocket; without the bit the slot stays inactive.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.numericSemantics: Bitmask, not a count. Bit n corresponds to pocket slot n, the same 0-based index as lbePocketIndex1..12; combine bits with OR.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.values: 0..4095 (12 slots); the shipped table uses values such as 15, 115, 2099 and 4067.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENTLIST/LOADBEARINGEQUI.source: game code (the pocket fallback and the attachment pocket lookup).

```

└── LOADBEARINGEQUIPMENT
```

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- [Items](Items.md) `ubClassIndex` is the row's position in this table; `lbeIndex` records that position but is not read by the game.
- `lbeClass` uses [Lookup.LBEClass](../Lookup.md#lbeclass), while the code enum `eLBE_CLASS` also defines `5` and `6`.
- `lbePocketIndex1..12` refer to [Pockets](Pockets.md); `0` leaves a slot inactive.
- `lbePocketsAvailable` bit `n` works together with `lbePocketIndex` slot `n`: the bit supplies the pocket from a worn LBE attachment when the slot itself has no pocket row.
- `lbeCombo` pairs this row with other LBE rows that may be worn at the same time.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: This table has no display strings; LBE names come from `Items`.

sections.heading: Versions

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- LBE table data.
- LBEClass lookup table.
- Game code: the LBE loader, the LBE and pocket structures, the item-size and volume calculations, and the inventory UI slot/pocket fallback.
- Field types are the storage types of the game structure, not the editor's generic `Integer` kind.
- Remaining statements about shipped values come from the XML data and are marked as such; they do not claim a code-verified formula.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- How a specific `lbeCombo` bit is assigned to a family of LBE pieces is a convention of the data author; the game only tests for a shared bit.
- The game picks an LBE row by its position in the list, so renumbering `lbeIndex` without keeping the rows in order would break the `Items.ubClassIndex` link; the table itself does not state that requirement.

tables/Items/Magazines.md.title: Magazines - magazines and ammo items
tables/Items/Magazines.md.summary: Magazines.xml defines ammo items: magazines, loose bullets, ammo boxes and crates. An item whose usItemClass is IC_AMMO points to a row through ubClassIndex; the row is stored in the runtime Magazine[] array. The row decides which weapon can load the item (ubCalibre, ubMagSize, ubAmmoType) and how the item behaves in bulk (ubMagType).

MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubAmmoType.description: Ammo type index into AmmoTypes. It selects the damage, armour interaction, tracer and other projectile properties.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubAmmoType.values: UINT8 index; valid IDs are the AmmoTypes rows.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubAmmoType.source: game code (magazine loader); related: Ammo and weapon damage dealt.

MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubCalibre.description: Calibre group of the ammo. The game uses it together with ubMagSize and ubAmmoType to find a matching magazine for a weapon and to name the calibre in the UI. It indexes the AmmoStrings list, which is filled in file order by the calibre loader (the uiIndex element is not read by that loader).
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubCalibre.values: UINT8 index; the AmmoStrings file supplies the name for each used calibre.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubCalibre.source: game code (magazine loader); related: Ammo and weapon damage dealt.

MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagSize.description: Capacity of the magazine in rounds. Loose bullets use 1; boxes and crates use a large capacity. The loader casts the value to UINT16.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagSize.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger quantity; negative values are not meaningful.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagSize.values: 0..65535; the loader casts the value to UINT16.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagSize.source: game code (magazine loader); related: Ammo and weapon damage dealt.

MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagType.description: Kind of ammo item. Values at or above AMMO_BOX are treated as bulk ammo and use different inventory, reload and transport rules.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/ubMagType.source: game code (magazine loader); related: Ammo and weapon damage dealt.

MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/uiIndex.description: XML identity and the index in the runtime Magazine[] array. Items uses ubClassIndex to point at this row for ammo items.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/uiIndex.default: none; a missing value leaves the array slot at zero.
MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE/uiIndex.source: game code (magazine loader); related: Ammo and weapon damage dealt.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Magazines.xml` defines ammo items: magazines, loose bullets, ammo boxes and crates. An item
whose `usItemClass` is `IC_AMMO` points to a row through `ubClassIndex`; the row is stored in
the runtime `Magazine[]` array. The row decides which weapon can load the item (`ubCalibre`,
`ubMagSize`, `ubAmmoType`) and how the item behaves in bulk (`ubMagType`).

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Magazines` | `Items/Magazines.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same schema; values may differ |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
MAGAZINELIST
└── MAGAZINE
    ├── uiIndex
    ├── ubCalibre
    ├── ubMagSize
    ├── ubAmmoType
    └── ubMagType
```

The loader writes each record to `Magazine[uiIndex]`. Records outside the array are ignored.
The editor key is `uiIndex`; after loading, the runtime `MAGTYPE.uiIndex` field is reused as a
back-reference to the owning item ID, so do not read the runtime field as the XML key.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- [Items](Items.md) `ubClassIndex` -> `Magazines.uiIndex` for `IC_AMMO` items.
- `Magazines.ubCalibre` -> [AmmoStrings](AmmoStrings.md) (calibre name), filled in file order.
- `Magazines.ubAmmoType` -> [AmmoTypes](AmmoTypes.md) `uiIndex`.
- `Magazines.ubMagType` -> [Lookup.MagazineType](../Lookup.md#magazinetype).
- [Weapons](Weapons.md) uses the same calibre/capacity/ammo type triple to find a magazine.

sections.heading: Related formulas
sections.text:
The ammo values feed a multi-stage damage pipeline documented in
[Related formulas](../../FORMULAS.md):

- [Armour protection](../../FORMULAS.md#armour-protection) - how `ubAmmoType` changes the
  protection value and armour wear.
- [Ammo and weapon damage dealt](../../FORMULAS.md#ammo-and-weapon-damage-dealt) - where
  `ubAmmoType` and the projectile count from the ammo type enter the damage result.

The field entries above define the inputs; they do not repeat the formulas.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
No strings in this table. Calibre names are in `AmmoStrings`, which the game's language
files provide; the table itself is not covered by `Russian.*` overlays.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
v4 and v5 use the same five fields and the same `MAGAZINELIST/MAGAZINE` structure. Values
differ; compare the files when a specific magazine matters.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: the magazine loader and the ammo/calibre lookup code.
- Table data: `Items/Magazines.xml`, `Items/AmmoStrings.xml`, `Items/AmmoTypes.xml`.
- Damage and armour interaction: [Related formulas](../../FORMULAS.md).

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `ubCalibre` is an index into a list filled in file order, not an explicit ID. Reordering
  `AmmoStrings.xml` would silently change every calibre name. This is a data-integrity risk
  worth reporting, but the loader is authoritative.
- The exact ammo match rule (calibre, capacity, ammo type) is in the item lookup code; this
  page documents the fields, not the search algorithm.

tables/Items/Merges.md.title: Merges - item merge recipes
tables/Items/Merges.md.summary: Merges.xml defines item-to-item recipes: two input items, up to two results, a merge type and an AP cost. The merge type selects the action and skill-check family.

MERGELIST/MERGE/APCost.numericSemantics: Action-point cost; the loader rescales it with DynamicAdjustAPConstants, so the stored value differs when AP_MAXIMUM is not 100.
MERGELIST/MERGE/APCost.values: 0..65535 after rescaling; the loader stores this field as UINT16.

tables/Items/PocketPopups.md.title: PocketPopups - NIV pocket menus
tables/Items/PocketPopups.md.summary: PocketPopups.xml defines the popup menu and nested submenus shown for a pocket in the New Inventory System. Each popup is built by a named generator rather than by a fixed item list.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/generator/id.description: A generator placed directly under POCKET instead of inside a popup wrapper. The loader only reads generator under popup or subMenu, so this element is ignored and creates no popup; the shipped data nevertheless contains such elements (for example pIndex 13, 14, 20 and 21).
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/generator/id.values: Any generator name; the loader does not consume it in this position.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/generator/id.default: empty string when omitted; no effect.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/generator/id.source: game code (pocket-popup loader); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pIndex.description: Pocket type that owns this popup definition. It is the key of the runtime LBEPocketPopup map, which the interface looks up with the pocket type returned for the slot; that value is also the pIndex of the corresponding Pockets row.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pIndex.values: 0..255; the loader casts the parsed value to UINT8. Shipped values are pocket-type IDs 1..22.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pIndex.default: 0 in the first record; a later record keeps the previous pocket ID when the element is omitted, because the parser does not reset the current ID per POCKET.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pIndex.source: game code (pocket-popup loader; pocket-type lookup); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pName.description: Pocket name present in the data. The pocket-popup loader does not read it, so it has no effect on the popup; where a pocket name is shown elsewhere (for example in Bobby Ray's LBE descriptions), it comes from Pockets.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/pName.source: game code (pocket-popup loader); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/generator/id.description: Generator that builds the top-level popup contents. The element may repeat, and each occurrence adds a generator to the popup. Unknown names silently map to no generator.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/generator/id.values: A generator name accepted by the loader: dummy, addArmor, addLBE, addWeapons, addWeaponGroups, addGrenades, addBombs, addFaceGear, addAmmo, addRifleGrenades, addRocketAmmo, addMisc or addKits; any other value (including none) adds nothing.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/generator/id.default: empty string when omitted; no generator is added.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/generator/id.source: game code (pocket-popup loader and generator registry); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/genera.description: Generator that builds the submenu contents. It uses the same name registry as the top-level generator, and unknown names add nothing.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/genera.default: empty string when omitted; no generator is added.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/genera.source: game code (pocket-popup loader and generator registry); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/name.description: Label of a submenu in the popup. The loader stores it in a 128-wide-character buffer (longer text is truncated) and applies it to the submenu option.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/name.values: Free text; the label is displayed in the popup.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/name.source: game code (pocket-popup loader; submenu renaming); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.description: Generator that builds the nested submenu contents. It uses the same name registry as the top-level generator, and unknown names add nothing.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.default: empty string when omitted; no generator is added.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.source: game code (pocket-popup loader and generator registry); pocket popup table data.

POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.description: Label of a nested submenu. Submenus may nest; the loader tracks up to POPUP_MAX_SUB_POPUPS (24) levels.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.values: Free text; the label is displayed in the nested popup.
POCKETPOPUPS/POCKET/popup/subMenu/subMen.source: game code (pocket-popup loader; nested submenu renaming); pocket popup table data.

POCKETLIST/POCKET/pRestriction.description: Bitmask of item classes the pocket accepts. Zero means the pocket has no class restriction.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pRestriction.numericSemantics: parsed with strtoul base 0, so decimal and 0x hexadecimal text are both accepted.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pRestriction.values: Bitmask of Lookup.ItemClass values (the IC_ bits stored in Items.usItemClass). 0 means no restriction; a non-zero mask must intersect the item class, otherwise the pocket accepts nothing.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pRestriction.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

POCKETLIST/POCKET/pSilhouette.description: Subimage index of the pocket silhouette in INTERFACE\Silhouettes.sti; it is drawn for an empty pocket.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pSilhouette.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pSilhouette.source: game code (Interface Items.cpp, Interface.cpp); table data.

POCKETLIST/POCKET/pType.description: Relative size weight of the pocket, used when an LBE item's size is recalculated from its contents. It is not the item-size capacity index; that is ItemCapacityPerSize.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pType.values: IDs from Lookup.PocketSize: 0 None, 1 Small, 2 Medium, 3 Large. 1, 2 and 3 are weighted as small/medium/large; 0 has no weight.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pType.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

POCKETLIST/POCKET/pVolume.description: Volume the pocket occupies on its LBE carrier. A pocket can be attached only while the carrier's free volume covers the sum of the attached pockets' volumes.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pVolume.numericSemantics: relative volume units; higher means a larger pocket, and negative values are impossible.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pVolume.values: 0..255; the sum is compared with LoadBearingEquipment.lbeAvailableVolume.
POCKETLIST/POCKET/pVolume.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `Pockets.xml` defines the pocket types used by the New Inventory System: the silhouette drawn for the empty pocket, the relative size weight, the accepted item classes, the volume the pocket takes on its carrier and the maximum number of items of each item size that fit. LBE items point at these rows through `lbePocketIndex*`.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `uiIndex` is referenced by `Items.randomitem` and by the `randomitem1..10` slots of other rows.
- `item1..10` refer to [Items](Items.md); an item that is itself a random item is expanded recursively instead of being added.
- `randomitem1..10` refer to other `RANDOMITEM` rows; their items are appended to the same candidate list rather than the category being chosen as one entry.
- A category already visited during the same lookup is not expanded again (taboo list), which prevents loops.
- Zero in any slot means the slot is empty. The item slots are expanded before the nested categories, and one entry is then chosen uniformly from the flattened list; duplicate entries are not removed.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The table has no weight field: selection is uniform over the flattened entries, so an item listed twice (directly or through two categories) is twice as likely. Whether modders expect that is not documented.
- A category referenced more than once is expanded only once per lookup because of the visited-class taboo list; the format does not document this.

tables/Items/StructureConstruct.md.title: StructureConstruct - buildable structures
tables/Items/StructureConstruct.md.summary: StructureConstruct.xml defines structures built from an item: the consumed item, its status loss, the tileset and facing tiles, the cost and the fortification adjustment.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/dCreationCost.description: Cost of building one structure, expressed in fortification work (progress) points. The cost is summed into the sector's maximum fortification progress when the plan is evaluated and is subtracted as each structure is built. It is not a money value.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/dCreationCost.numericSemantics: Fractional progress points; higher values mean more work. The loader stores the parsed value without clamping or rejecting it.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/dCreationCost.default: 1.0 from the STRUCTURE_CONSTRUCT constructor when omitted. An empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/dCreationCost.source: game code (structure-construct loader; fortification progress accounting and consumption); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/eastfacingtile.description: Tile index in the tileset used when the builder faces east. The element may repeat; the game picks one entry at random from this list.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/eastfacingtile.numericSemantics: Index within the tileset; 0..255. The union of the four facing lists is the set of structures offered in the fortification build menu. A build for a cardinal direction needs that direction's list; for a diagonal facing the game tries north, then south, then west, then east. When fFortifyAdjacentAdjustment is set, the lists also supply the compatible variants for adjacent nodes.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/eastfacingtile.default: Empty list when omitted (not 0); an empty element adds index 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/eastfacingtile.source: game code (structure-construct loader; fortification build selection); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/fFortifyAdjacen.description: If set, the game tries to make a newly built fortification node match adjacent nodes of the same construct row by choosing compatible direction variants from the facing-tile lists.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/fFortifyAdjacen.default: 1 (TRUE) from the STRUCTURE_CONSTRUCT constructor when omitted. An empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/fFortifyAdjacen.source: game code (structure-construct loader; adjacent-node adjustment); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/northfacingtile.description: Tile index in the tileset used when the builder faces north. The element may repeat; the game picks one entry at random from this list.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/northfacingtile.numericSemantics: Index within the tileset; 0..255. The union of the four facing lists is the set of structures offered in the fortification build menu. A build for a cardinal direction needs that direction's list; for a diagonal facing the game tries north, then south, then west, then east. When fFortifyAdjacentAdjustment is set, the lists also supply the compatible variants for adjacent nodes.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/northfacingtile.default: Empty list when omitted (not 0); an empty element adds index 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/northfacingtile.source: game code (structure-construct loader; fortification build selection); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/southfacingtile.numericSemantics: Index within the tileset; 0..255. The union of the four facing lists is the set of structures offered in the fortification build menu. A build for a cardinal direction needs that direction's list; for a diagonal facing the game tries north, then south, then west, then east. When fFortifyAdjacentAdjustment is set, the lists also supply the compatible variants for adjacent nodes.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/southfacingtile.default: Empty list when omitted (not 0); an empty element adds index 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/southfacingtile.source: game code (structure-construct loader; fortification build selection); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetDispla.description: Player-facing name of the structure, listed in the fortification build menu for construct entries whose tileset is available in the current tileset set (or in the generic set).
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetDispla.values: Free text; stored in a 20-byte buffer without appending a terminator, so longer text is truncated and may fill the buffer.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetDispla.source: game code (structure-construct loader; fortification build-menu list); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.description: Tileset file name whose tiles represent the structure. It is matched case-insensitively against a prefix of the tileset's tile-surface file names: 10 characters in the hand-build path and 11 in the build-menu and plan paths.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.values: Free text such as sandbag.sti; stored in a 20-byte buffer without appending a terminator, so longer text is truncated.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.default: Empty string when omitted; an empty name matches no tileset.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.source: game code (structure-construct loader; tileset matching); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreationItem.values: Item ID; 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreationItem.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreationItem.source: game code (structure-construct loader; construction item consumption); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemStatusLos.description: Item status (condition) removed from the creation item each time the structure is built. If the item's remaining status is less than or equal to this value, the item is deleted instead of reduced.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemStatusLos.numericSemantics: Percentage points of item condition on the objectStatus scale. 0 means the item is not damaged.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemStatusLos.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8, and the item code treats it as a condition percentage (0..100 is the normal range).
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemStatusLos.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemStatusLos.source: game code (structure-construct loader; construction item consumption and fortification resource consumption); structure construction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.default: Empty string when omitted; an empty name matches no tileset.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/szTileSetName.source: game code (structure-deconstruct loader; tileset matching); structure deconstruction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreatedItemSt.description: Condition given to the created item, in item-status (condition) percent. A value of 0 means no item is created; a non-zero value is passed to item creation as the starting condition.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreatedItemSt.numericSemantics: Percentage points of item condition on the objectStatus scale. The item-creation call guards against zero with max(1, status), but the stored value is an unsigned byte, so a non-zero value is already at least 1.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreatedItemSt.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8, and the item code treats it as a condition percentage (0..100 is the normal range).
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreatedItemSt.default: 0 when omitted (no item is created); an empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usCreatedItemSt.source: game code (structure-deconstruct loader; item creation on deconstruction); structure deconstruction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usDeconstructIt.description: Item ID required to deconstruct the structure. A value of 0 matches no real item, so it disables item-based deconstruction for the row.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usDeconstructIt.values: Item ID; 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usDeconstructIt.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usDeconstructIt.source: game code (structure-deconstruct loader; deconstruction item matching); structure deconstruction table data.

STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemToCreate.description: Item ID created when the structure is deconstructed. The item is created only when both this field and usCreatedItemStatus are non-zero.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemToCreate.values: Item ID; 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemToCreate.default: 0 when omitted (no item is created); an empty element is parsed as 0.
STRUCTURESLIST/STRUCTURE/usItemToCreate.source: game code (structure-deconstruct loader; deconstruction result); structure deconstruction table data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `StructureDeconstruct.xml` defines how a structure is removed and what item it yields: the tool item, the created item and status, the tileset, the cost and the allowed tiles.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `StructureDeconstruct` | `Items/StructureDeconstruct.xml` | v4 and v5 have the same field paths; values differ. `allowedtile` repeats. |

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
STRUCTURESLIST
└── STRUCTURE
    ├── usDeconstructItem
    ├── usItemToCreate
    ├── usCreatedItemStatus
    ├── szTileSetDisplayName
    ├── szTileSetName
    ├── dCreationCost
    └── allowedtile
```

`STRUCTURESLIST` has no key element. The loader stores rows in document order; a row is
selected by the held deconstruction item (`usDeconstructItem`) and then checked against the
tileset name and allowed structure number, or, for automatic fortification removal, by the
tileset name with the structure number deciding whether removal is allowed.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `usDeconstructItem` and `usItemToCreate` point to [Items](Items.md).
- The tileset columns refer to structures in the named tileset, not to item rows.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
`szTileSetDisplayName` is intended as the player-facing structure name, but no consumer was
found in this source tree; `szTileSetName` is an asset key.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Structure deconstruction table data.
- Game code: structure-deconstruct loader, deconstruction item matching, item creation, fortification progress accounting.
- Defaults from the `STRUCTURE_DECONSTRUCT` record.
- Descriptions cover the values the code reads, stores and uses; every field in this document is backed by the loader.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- Whether `szTileSetDisplayName` is used by any UI outside this source tree is unknown; no read of it was found in the shipped code.
- The number of construction points generated per assignment work tick, and therefore the practical balance of `dCreationCost` values, is defined by the assignment system outside this table.
