tables/Items/Weapons.md.title: Weapons - weapon statistics
tables/Items/Weapons.md.summary: Weapons.xml holds the combat and presentation statistics of every weapon. Items points to a weapon row through ubClassIndex; the row feeds AP costs, accuracy, range, sound selection, burst behaviour and the item description panel.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReload.description: Base AP cost of a normal reload. The loader rescales it to AP_MAXIMUM; GetAPsToReload applies the per-type reload modifier and the reload-time reduction.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReload.numericSemantics: Action-point cost; higher values mean a more expensive reload.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReload.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReload.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReload.source: game code (weapon loader; GetAPsToReload); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReloadManually.description: AP cost to chamber or pump a round when the weapon has ammunition but no cartridge in the chamber (manual action). It is not the cost of a full reload.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReloadManually.numericSemantics: Action-point cost; the loader rescales it to AP_MAXIMUM, and the game applies the per-type manual-reload modifier and the Sniper/Ranger trait reductions.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReloadManually.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReloadManually.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/APsToReloadManually.source: game code (weapon loader; GetAPsToAutoReload chambering path); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/AutoPenalty.description: Accuracy penalty applied to autofire. It is subtracted from the OCTH chance to hit once per extra shot in the volley.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/AutoPenalty.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a stronger penalty; 0 means no autofire penalty. The game reduces it by the auto-to-hit bonus and clamps the result at 0.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/AutoPenalty.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/AutoPenalty.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/AutoPenalty.source: game code (weapon loader; OCTH autofire accuracy); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BarrelConfiguration.description: Number of barrels/projectiles in one barrel configuration. The element may repeat to describe several configurations; each nonzero value is a selectable barrel count. Only weapons with the IC_BOBBY_GUN class use it.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BarrelConfiguration.values: 1..255; the loader skips 0 entries. If no nonzero value is present, one barrel is assumed.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BarrelConfiguration.default: absent or all-zero means one barrel; repeated elements add barrel configurations.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BarrelConfiguration.source: game code (weapon loader; GetFittingBarrelMode/GetNextBarrelMode); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BurstAniDelay.description: Per-frame animation delay used while a burst-fire animation plays. It is stored in WEAPONTYPE.sAniDelay and copied to the soldier's animation delay.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BurstAniDelay.numericSemantics: Time value; higher values play the burst animation more slowly.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BurstAniDelay.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/BurstAniDelay.source: game code (weapon loader; soldier animation delay); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/EasyUnjam.description: If set, unjamming uses a fixed +100 skill-check modifier instead of the reliability-based modifier, so the check is capped at 99% and effectively always succeeds. No experience is awarded for unjamming such a weapon.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/EasyUnjam.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/EasyUnjam.source: game code (weapon loader; unjam skill check); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/Handling.description: Weapon-handling difficulty used by NCTH. Higher values raise the gun-difficulty term in CalcNewChanceToHitGun, which lowers the chance to hit.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/Handling.numericSemantics: Higher values represent a weapon that is harder to control; lower values are easier.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/Handling.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/Handling.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/Handling.source: game code (weapon loader; NCTH handling difficulty); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/HeavyGun.description: Marks a two-handed weapon as heavy. While standing it must be fired from the hip (alternative weapon holding) and cannot be shouldered; the flag is consulted by the alternative-holding logic, not by strength or bipod checks.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/HeavyGun.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/HeavyGun.source: game code (weapon loader; alternative weapon-holding and aim-level logic); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ManualReloadSound.description: Sound ID played while a round is manually chambered or pumped.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ManualReloadSound.values: Sound ID; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ManualReloadSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ManualReloadSound.source: game code (weapon loader; manual-reload sound); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/MaxDistForMessyDeath.description: Maximum distance at which head and torso hits can trigger the instant-kill and messy-death special effects (head explosion, chest explosion). Beyond this distance those specials do not trigger.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/MaxDistForMessyDeath.numericSemantics: Higher values allow the specials at a longer range; 0 restricts them to the same tile. For guns, the value is scaled by the per-weapon-type distance modifier before the range test.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/MaxDistForMessyDeath.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/MaxDistForMessyDeath.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/MaxDistForMessyDeath.source: game code (weapon loader; CalcChanceToHitGun hit-location specials); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/NoSemiAuto.description: If set, the weapon has no semi-automatic fire mode; switching to it selects autofire.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/NoSemiAuto.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/NoSemiAuto.source: game code (weapon loader; weapon-mode selection); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SilencedSound.description: Sound ID played instead of sSound when the shot is treated as silenced (noise below the configured threshold, or ubAttackVolume at most 10). The game plays it directly, with no 0 guard and no fallback to sSound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SilencedSound.values: Sound ID; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SilencedSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SilencedSound.source: game code (weapon loader; silenced shot sound); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SwapClips.description: If set, a same-size, same-ammo reload in turn-based combat uses a magazine swap (RELOAD_SWAP) instead of topping the weapon off round by round; a wrong-size magazine then uses the AP_WRONG_MAG cost. If clear, a same-size, same-ammo reload tops the weapon off; a different ammo type still swaps the magazine.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SwapClips.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/SwapClips.source: game code (weapon loader; reload-type selection); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAccuracy.description: Old Chance to Hit (OCTH) accuracy value. nAccuracy is the NCTH counterpart.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAccuracy.numericSemantics: Higher values make the weapon more accurate; lower values make it less accurate, and negative values act as an accuracy penalty.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAccuracy.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAccuracy.source: game code (weapon loader; OCTH hit calculation); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAutofireShotsPerFiveA.description: Number of autofire shots per five AP. It is a rate value, not a magazine capacity; 0 disables autofire.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAutofireShotsPerFiveA.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a faster autofire rate. The game multiplies the value by the per-type INI modifier, adds bAutofireBulletsPer5APModifier, and clamps the result to at least 1 when the base value is positive.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAutofireShotsPerFiveA.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAutofireShotsPerFiveA.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bAutofireShotsPerFiveA.source: game code (weapon loader; GetAutofireShotsPerFiveAPs and autofire AP cost); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bBurstAP.description: Base AP cost of a burst. The loader rescales it from the 100-AP baseline to AP_MAXIMUM, and CalcAPsToBurst scales it by the shooter's action points and applies burst AP reductions.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bBurstAP.numericSemantics: Action-point cost; higher values mean a more expensive burst.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bBurstAP.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bBurstAP.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bBurstAP.source: game code (weapon loader; CalcAPsToBurst); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilX.description: Horizontal recoil deviation used by NCTH. Positive values kick right; the final value is clamped to at least 0, so a negative configured value does not produce a leftward kick.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilX.numericSemantics: A larger value is harder to control. Shipped values are non-negative; the metadata allows -20..20, but GetRecoil clamps the result at 0.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilX.values: -20..20 in the metadata; observed values are 0..4.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilX.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilX.source: game code (weapon loader; GetRecoil); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilY.description: Vertical recoil deviation used by NCTH. Positive values kick up; the final value is clamped to at least 0, so a negative configured value does not produce a downward kick.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilY.numericSemantics: A larger value is harder to control. Shipped values are non-negative; the metadata allows -20..20, but GetRecoil clamps the result at 0.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilY.values: -20..20 in the metadata; observed values are 0..14.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilY.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/bRecoilY.source: game code (weapon loader; GetRecoil); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/fBurstOnlyByFanTheHamm.description: If set, burst mode is available only to a gunslinger using the weapon in hip-fire. The condition is part of the weapon's fire-mode rules, not a UI preference: it requires the new trait system, the fan-the-hammer option, the GUNSLINGER trait, alternative weapon holding and an empty second hand.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/fBurstOnlyByFanTheHamm.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/fBurstOnlyByFanTheHamm.source: game code (weapon loader; IsGunBurstCapable and alternative holding); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/nAccuracy.description: New Chance to Hit (NCTH) accuracy value. bAccuracy is the OCTH counterpart.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/nAccuracy.numericSemantics: Higher values make the weapon more accurate; lower values make it less accurate, and negative values act as an accuracy penalty.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/nAccuracy.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8 and the field metadata declares no narrower range.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/nAccuracy.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/nAccuracy.source: game code (weapon loader; NCTH accuracy); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sBurstSound.description: Index into the gzBurstSndStrings[] filename templates used for the burst sound in the original (non-NWSS) sound system. It is not a PlayJA2Sample sound ID; 0 means no burst sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sBurstSound.values: Index into the burst-sound template table; 0 disables the burst sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sBurstSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sBurstSound.source: game code (weapon loader; original burst sound path); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sLocknLoadSound.description: Sound ID played while a round is chambered or the weapon is readied. 0 suppresses the sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sLocknLoadSound.values: Sound ID; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sLocknLoadSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sLocknLoadSound.source: game code (weapon loader; lock-and-load animation); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sReloadSound.description: Sound ID played while reloading. 0 suppresses the reload sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sReloadSound.values: Sound ID; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sReloadSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sReloadSound.source: game code (weapon loader; reload sound selection); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSilencedBurstSound.description: Index into the gzBurstSndStrings[] filename templates used for the silenced burst sound in the original (non-NWSS) sound system. It is not a PlayJA2Sample sound ID; 0 means no silenced burst sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSilencedBurstSound.values: Index into the burst-sound template table; 0 disables the silenced burst sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSilencedBurstSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSilencedBurstSound.source: game code (weapon loader; original silenced burst sound path); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSound.description: Sound ID played for a normal shot. 0 (NO_WEAPON_SOUND) suppresses the shot sound.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSound.values: Sound ID; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSound.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/sSound.source: game code (weapon loader; shot sound selection); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szNWSSSound.description: Base name used by the New Weapon Sound System. The game builds a file name from the calibre, this name and the shot variant (loop, single, or a room/echo variant); when the name is empty or the file does not exist it falls back to the weapon-type name and then to the generic file.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szNWSSSound.values: Free text, truncated to MAX_WEAPON_NAME_LENGTH (20) characters.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szNWSSSound.source: game code (weapon loader; NWSS filename construction); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szWeaponName.description: Name stored in WEAPONTYPE.szWeaponName. No gameplay or interface code reads it; weapon display names come from the item master table.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szWeaponName.values: Free text, truncated to MAX_WEAPON_NAME_LENGTH (20) characters.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/szWeaponName.source: game code (weapon loader); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAimLevels.description: Number of aim levels available to the weapon in NCTH. A value outside 1..8 makes the game fall back to its class-and-range algorithm; the runtime result is always clamped to 1..8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAimLevels.numericSemantics: Higher values allow more aiming levels (finer aim); 0 or any value above 8 means automatic. Non-gun weapons use a fixed base of 2, and the Throwing trait can reduce the throwing-knife value further (minimum 1).
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAimLevels.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAimLevels.source: game code (weapon loader; AllowedAimingLevelsNCTH); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAttackVolume.description: Noise volume produced by firing the weapon. It feeds sound propagation and AI hearing checks through MakeNoise.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAttackVolume.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a louder shot; 0 makes the shot silent to the noise system.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAttackVolume.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAttackVolume.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubAttackVolume.source: game code (weapon loader; firing noise); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBulletSpeed.description: Controls the bullet's on-screen travel rate. The game divides it (plus the attachment/ammo bullet-speed bonus) by 10 and uses the result as the per-tile update interval; it does not affect damage or hit probability.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBulletSpeed.numericSemantics: A larger value produces a longer interval between one-tile steps, so the projectile appears slower despite the field name. A value of 0 gives a near-instant visual bullet.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBulletSpeed.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBulletSpeed.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBulletSpeed.source: game code (weapon loader; bullet travel interval); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBurstPenalty.description: Accuracy penalty applied to burst fire. It is subtracted from the OCTH chance to hit once per shot after the first.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBurstPenalty.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a stronger penalty for each extra shot in the burst; the game reduces it by the burst-to-hit bonus and clamps the result at 0.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBurstPenalty.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBurstPenalty.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubBurstPenalty.source: game code (weapon loader; OCTH burst accuracy); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubCalibre.description: Calibre index. It is compared with Magazines.ubCalibre for ammunition compatibility and indexes the AmmoCaliber and NWSSCaliber strings in AmmoStrings.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubCalibre.values: Index of a row in AmmoStrings; 0 is the empty calibre.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubCalibre.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubCalibre.source: game code (weapon loader; ammunition matching and AmmoCaliber lookup); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubDeadliness.description: Comparative deadliness rating used for a mercenary's gun attractiveness, AI threat evaluation and item valuation. It is not a direct damage value.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubDeadliness.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a more desirable or threatening weapon; the value is a rating, not a damage amount.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubDeadliness.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubDeadliness.source: game code (weapon loader; mercenary profile and AI threat code); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubHitVolume.description: Noise volume produced when a bullet strikes a target or structure, passed to MakeNoise with NOISE_BULLET_IMPACT. It is not a hit-resolution or accuracy value.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubHitVolume.numericSemantics: Higher values make bullet impacts louder to the noise system; 0 makes them silent.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubHitVolume.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubHitVolume.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubHitVolume.source: game code (weapon loader; bullet-impact noise); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubImpact.description: Base damage of the weapon before item, ammunition and attachment damage bonuses, range modifiers and armour reduction.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubImpact.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a stronger base hit; the final damage is clamped to 255 by GetDamage.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubImpact.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubImpact.source: game code (weapon loader; GetDamage/GetBasicDamage); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubMagSize.description: Base magazine capacity used when the weapon is loaded. GetMagSize adds the attachment magazine bonus; this field describes the weapon's magazine, not the magazine item row.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubMagSize.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a larger capacity; 0 leaves the weapon dependent on an attachment-provided magazine.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubMagSize.values: 0..65000; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubMagSize.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubMagSize.source: game code (weapon loader; GetMagSize); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubReadyTime.description: AP cost to ready the weapon before firing. It is separate from the AP cost of the shot itself.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubReadyTime.numericSemantics: Action-point cost, not a time. The loader rescales it from the 100-AP baseline to the configured AP_MAXIMUM with DynamicAdjustAPConstants; higher values mean a more expensive ready.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubReadyTime.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubReadyTime.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubReadyTime.source: game code (weapon loader; AP constants); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubRecoilDelay.description: Number of leading bullets in a volley that produce no recoil. GetRecoil returns zero while the bullet number is at most this value.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubRecoilDelay.numericSemantics: Higher values make the first few shots of a burst recoil-free; 0 gives only the first bullet no recoil.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubRecoilDelay.values: 0..5 in the metadata; observed values are 0, 2 and 3.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubRecoilDelay.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubRecoilDelay.source: game code (weapon loader; GetRecoil); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPer4Turns.description: Mechanical rate of fire expressed as shots per four turns. The game derives the AP cost from this value and the weapon's AP settings; it is not a direct "shots per turn" counter.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPer4Turns.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a faster mechanical rate of fire (more shots per four turns) and therefore a lower AP cost per shot in BaseAPsToShootOrStab. The effective value must be positive; 0 makes the AP calculation return -1 (invalid).
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPer4Turns.values: Decimal number; shipped values are positive for weapons and 0 for the placeholder row.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPer4Turns.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPer4Turns.source: game code (weapon loader and AP calculation); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPerBurst.description: Base number of projectiles fired by one burst. The runtime value is GetShotsPerBurst, which adds the attachment burst-size bonus.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPerBurst.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more projectiles in a burst; 0 means the weapon has no burst mode unless an attachment grants one.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPerBurst.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPerBurst.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubShotsPerBurst.source: game code (weapon loader; GetShotsPerBurst); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponClass.description: Broad weapon class used by dealer and interface filters and by class comparisons such as handgun, SMG, shotgun, knife and monster. It is coarser than ubWeaponType.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponClass.values: IDs from Lookup.WeaponClass: 0 None, 1 Handgun, 2 Submachinegun, 3 Rifle, 4 Machinegun, 5 Shotgun, 6 Knife, 7 Monster.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponClass.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponClass.source: game code (weapon loader and WeaponClass checks); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponType.description: Specific weapon type within the class, used for per-type item modifiers, AI weapon preference and interface grouping.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponType.values: IDs from Lookup.WeaponType: 0 None, 1 Pistol, 2 Machine Pistol, 3 Submachinegun, 4 Rifle, 5 Sniper Rifle, 6 Assault Rifle, 7 Light Machinegun, 8 Shotgun.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponType.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/ubWeaponType.source: game code (weapon loader and WeaponType enum); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/uiIndex.description: Index of the weapon row in the runtime weapon table and the identity of the XML record. Items.ubClassIndex of a weapon item points here.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/uiIndex.values: 0..16000; the loader writes into Weapon[MAXITEMS] with MAXITEMS = 16001, and rows with a larger uiIndex are silently ignored.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/uiIndex.default: missing or empty means 0; the parser zeroes the record, so such a row is stored at index 0.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/uiIndex.source: game code (weapon loader and runtime Weapon array); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingDamageThr.description: Temperature at which the weapon starts to take damage in the overheating model. The game compares it with bTemperature and returns the ratio as a damage percentage.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingDamageThr.numericSemantics: Temperature value on the 0..OVERHEATING_MAX_TEMPERATURE scale (60000); higher values tolerate more heat before damage.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingDamageThr.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingDamageThr.source: game code (weapon loader; GetOverheatDamageThreshold); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingJamThresh.description: Temperature at which the weapon starts to jam in the overheating model. The game compares it with bTemperature and returns the ratio as a jam percentage.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingJamThresh.numericSemantics: Temperature value on the 0..OVERHEATING_MAX_TEMPERATURE scale (60000); higher values tolerate more heat before jamming.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingJamThresh.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingJamThresh.source: game code (weapon loader; GetOverheatJamThreshold); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingSingleSho.description: Temperature added by one shot in the overheating model. Attachments and ammunition can modify it at use.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingSingleSho.numericSemantics: Temperature value on the 0..OVERHEATING_MAX_TEMPERATURE scale (60000); higher values add more heat per shot.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingSingleSho.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usOverheatingSingleSho.source: game code (weapon loader; GetSingleShotTemperature); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usRange.description: Effective range in world units, where 10 units equal one tile. GunRange and InRange compare it with the distance after applying range bonuses.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usRange.numericSemantics: Higher values mean a longer range; 0 makes the base range 0, although GunRange can still add flat range bonuses.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usRange.values: 0..5000; the loader stores this field as UINT16.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usRange.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usRange.source: game code (weapon loader; GunRange/GetModifiedGunRange); weapon table data.

WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usReloadDelay.description: Delay of the reload animation. The game adds it to MANDATORY_WEAPON_DELAY when it sets the soldier's reload delay; it is a presentation/timing value, not the AP cost of reloading.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usReloadDelay.numericSemantics: Time value; higher values mean a longer reload animation.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usReloadDelay.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
WEAPONLIST/WEAPON/usReloadDelay.source: game code (weapon loader; reload animation timing); weapon table data.

sections.heading: Game options
sections.text: `bAccuracy`, `ubBurstPenalty` and `AutoPenalty` belong to Old Chance to Hit (OCTH). `nAccuracy`, `bRecoilX`, `bRecoilY`, `ubAimLevels`, `ubRecoilDelay` and `Handling` belong to New Chance to Hit (NCTH). NCTH is forced off in multiplayer, even when the option is enabled. See [OPTIONS](../../OPTIONS.md#chance-to-hit-ncth-and-octh).

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- [Items](Items.md) `ubClassIndex` of a weapon item points to `Weapons.uiIndex`.
- `ubCalibre` points to [AmmoStrings](AmmoStrings.md) and is compared with `Magazines.ubCalibre`; the calibre label is display data, while ammunition behaviour comes from [AmmoTypes](AmmoTypes.md) and the [Magazines](Magazines.md) row.
- `Magazines.ubAmmoType` selects the ammo behaviour loaded by a magazine; `Weapons.ubCalibre` only selects the calibre family.
- NCTH fields are read only when the new chance-to-hit system is active; OCTH uses `bAccuracy`, `ubBurstPenalty` and `AutoPenalty`.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: The calibre label comes from `AmmoStrings` and is localized there. `szWeaponName` is stored but not displayed; weapon display names live in the item master table. Numeric sound and lookup IDs are not localized.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same 48 field paths. `BarrelConfiguration` is repeated in both versions. In the reference data the values are identical apart from one extra weapon record in v4.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text: No unresolved field semantics remain. The only design-level oddity is `ubBulletSpeed`: the code uses the value as a per-tile update interval (larger values slow the visual projectile), which is opposite to what the field name suggests.

tables/Lookup.md.title: Lookup tables
tables/Lookup.md.summary: The Lookup directory contains small dictionaries that turn numeric values into labels for the editor and for modders. They are editor-side data: the game code does not read these files, it uses the numeric constants that the values mirror. The editor uses them for combo boxes, bit editors and the "where used" views.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the value. For flag lookups this is a bit or a combination of bits; for sequence lookups it is an ordinal or an explicit ID.
id.default: none; the value must exist in the file.
id.source: lookup XML data; editor metadata for flag/sequence kind.

name.description: Display label for the value, shown in editor combo boxes and bit lists. For a combined flag value it describes the group of bits.
name.values: free text; unique within one lookup in practice.
name.source: lookup XML data; editor metadata for flag/sequence kind.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
The `Lookup` directory contains small dictionaries that turn numeric values into labels for
the editor and for modders. They are **editor-side data**: the game code does not read these
files, it uses the numeric constants that the values mirror. The editor uses them for combo
boxes, bit editors and the "where used" views.

The lookups share one structure. Each is either a flag/bitmask dictionary
(`IsFlagLookup = 1`) or a sequential value list. The files parse in both v4 and v5;
`Lookup/AttachmentPoint.xml` was repaired on 2026-11-07.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
All lookup files use `JA2Data` as the document root and the lookup name as the record
element (`AmmoChoices`, `ItemClass`, ...).

| Lookup | File | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AmmoChoices` | `Lookup/AmmoChoices.xml` | sequence | sparse IDs for enemy/militia ammo choices |
| `AmmoFlag` | `Lookup/AmmoFlag.xml` | flags | ammo property bits |
| `ArmourClass` | `Lookup/ArmourClass.xml` | sequence | matches `ARMOURCLASS_*` |
| `AttachmentClass` | `Lookup/AttachmentClass.xml` | flags | OAS attachment classes |
| `AttachmentPoint` | `Lookup/AttachmentPoint.xml` | flags | v5 repaired file |
| `AttachmentSystem` | `Lookup/AttachmentSystem.xml` | sequence | Any / OAS / NAS |
| `Cursor` | `Lookup/Cursor.xml` | sequence | cursor IDs |
| `DrugType` | `Lookup/DrugType.xml` | flags | drug effect bits |
| `ExplosionSize` | `Lookup/ExplosionSize.xml` | sequence | explosion size |
| `ExplosionType` | `Lookup/ExplosionType.xml` | sequence | explosion kind |
| `ItemClass` | `Lookup/ItemClass.xml` | flags | `IC_*` bit flags |
| `ItemFlag` | `Lookup/ItemFlag.xml` | flags | item flags, 64-bit |
| `LBEClass` | `Lookup/LBEClass.xml` | sequence | load-bearing equipment class |
| `MagazineType` | `Lookup/MagazineType.xml` | sequence | magazine / bullet / box / crate |
| `MergeType` | `Lookup/MergeType.xml` | sequence | merge transformation kind |
| `NasAttachmentClass` | `Lookup/NasAttachmentClass.xml` | flags | NAS attachment classes |
| `NasLayoutClass` | `Lookup/NasLayoutClass.xml` | flags | NAS layout classes |
| `PocketSize` | `Lookup/PocketSize.xml` | sequence | pocket size |

sections.heading: Lookup details
sections.text:
Each entry repeats the kind and the source of its values. The full value lists stay in the
XML files; the editor and the future help window read them from there.

### AmmoChoices

Sequence lookup with sparse IDs. Used by enemy/militia ammo choice tables,
not by the item data directly.

### AmmoFlag

Flag lookup. Ammo property bits used by `AmmoTypes.ammoflag`.

### ArmourClass

Sequence lookup. Matches `ARMOURCLASS_*`; used by
[Armours](Items/Armours.md).

### AttachmentClass

Flag lookup. OAS attachment class bits.

### AttachmentPoint

Flag lookup. Used by the attachment slot
and NAS fields.

### AttachmentSystem

Sequence lookup: Any, OAS only, NAS only.

### Cursor

Sequence lookup. Cursor IDs used by the UI.

### DrugType

Flag lookup. Drug effect bits used by `Drugs`.

### ExplosionSize

Sequence lookup, from none to large.

### ExplosionType

Sequence lookup, such as normal, stun and tear gas.

### ItemClass

Flag lookup. `IC_*` item class bits.

### ItemFlag

Flag lookup. Item flags, including 64-bit values.

### LBEClass

Sequence lookup. Load-bearing equipment class.

### MagazineType

Sequence lookup: magazine, bullet(s), box, crate. Matches `AMMO_MAGAZINE`,
`AMMO_BULLET`, `AMMO_BOX`, `AMMO_CRATE`; used by [Magazines](Items/Magazines.md).

### MergeType

Sequence lookup. Merge/transformation kind.

### NasAttachmentClass

Flag lookup. NAS attachment class bits.

### NasLayoutClass

Flag lookup. NAS layout class bits.

### PocketSize

Sequence lookup: none, small, medium, large.

### Separability

Sequence lookup: removable, inseparable, replaceable.

### Silhouette

Sequence lookup. Item silhouette used by the inventory display.

### SkillCheckType

Sequence lookup. Skill check kind.

### WeaponClass

Sequence lookup. `WEAPONCLASS_*` used by `Weapons.ubWeaponClass`.

### WeaponType

Sequence lookup. `WEAPONTYPE_*` used by `Weapons.ubWeaponType`.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
JA2Data
├── id
└── name
```

- `id` may be sparse (`AmmoChoices` uses 19, 29, ... 79).
- `name` is a label, not a localization key. Names are English and are not translated by
  `Russian.*` overlays.
- Flag lookups may contain combined values in `id`; a row can document a group of bits as
  well as a single bit.
- Record order is not significant; the editor sorts by `id`.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
The lookups mirror numeric constants used by item and weapon fields. Examples:

- `Items.usItemClass` and `Items.<flag fields>` use `ItemClass` and
  `ItemFlag`.
- `Weapons.ubWeaponClass` / `ubWeaponType` use `WeaponClass` and
  `WeaponType`.
- `Armours.ubArmourClass` uses `ArmourClass`.
- `Magazines.ubMagType` uses `MagazineType`.

The table documents are the authority for which field uses which lookup; this page only
defines the dictionaries.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
Lookup names are not translated by the game's overlay mechanism. A Russian UI may translate
the label shown around a lookup, but the `name` values in these files stay English.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
- v4 and v5 have the same lookup files and the same `id`/`name` schema.
- `Lookup/AttachmentPoint.xml` in v5 was repaired on 2026-11-07; it now parses and contains
  the attachment-point values:

| id | name |
|---:|---|
| 0 | None |
| 1 | Small Molle |
| 2 | Medium Molle |
| 3 | All Molle |
| 4 | Hydration Carrier |
| 7 | All Molle and Carrier |
| 8 | Surgical Mask and Gloves |
| 16 | Batteries |

The repair is a data fix, not a code change. `help-inventory.ps1` still falls back to v4 if
a future v5 file fails to parse; the fallback is not used by the current v5 tree.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- `TableData/Lookup/*.xml` (v4 and v5) - the values and names.
- `metadata: Tables.IsFlagLookup` - flag vs sequence classification.
- Game constants that the values mirror: item classes and flags, armour classes, weapon
  classes and types, ammo flags, and skill-check kinds.
- No game loader reads `TableData/Lookup/*.xml`; they are editor/modding data.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- Do all lookup ID sets exactly match the current code constants? The B0 pass verified
  counts, kinds and ranges, but not every constant against its header.
- Should combined flag rows be listed as separate values or kept only in the lookup file?
  The editor shows them as values; the documents do not duplicate the full value list.

tables/Map/AltSectors.md.summary: AltSectors.xml is a 16×16 matrix. Each ROW element has a y attribute for the map row and 16 values, one per map column. A non-zero value selects the alternate-sector group used for that sector.

ALT_SECTORS_LIST/ROW.description: One row of the alternate-sector matrix. The row is taken from the y attribute (letter A..P or a number); the element text is read as a whitespace-separated sequence of numeric values, one per column, and written into the row starting at column 1. 0 means no alternate sector.
ALT_SECTORS_LIST/ROW.numericSemantics: Values are alternate-sector IDs, so larger is not “more”; 0 = none.
ALT_SECTORS_LIST/ROW.values: Up to 16 numeric values per row; the loader does not validate the count.
ALT_SECTORS_LIST/ROW.default: Required; one row of the map.
ALT_SECTORS_LIST/ROW.source: game code (alternate-sector loader); map table data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `BloodcatPlacements.xml` lists sectors where bloodcats can appear. Each sector has one placement type and, for each difficulty, values for the group size, ambush chance, faction affiliation and respawn; which of those values matter depends on the placement type.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
BLOODCAT_PLACEMENTS
└── SECTOR
    ├── SectorGrid
    ├── ubPlacementType
    ├── NOVICE
    │   ├── fRespawn
    │   ├── ubAmbushChance
    │   ├── ubFactionAffiliation
    │   ├── ubMinBloodcats
    │   └── ubMaxBloodcats
    ├── EXPERIENCED
    │   ├── fRespawn
    │   ├── ubAmbushChance
    │   ├── ubFactionAffiliation
    │   ├── ubMinBloodcats
    │   └── ubMaxBloodcats
    ├── EXPERT
    │   ├── fRespawn
    │   ├── ubAmbushChance
    │   ├── ubFactionAffiliation
    │   ├── ubMinBloodcats
    │   └── ubMaxBloodcats
    └── INSANE
        ├── fRespawn
        ├── ubAmbushChance
        ├── ubFactionAffiliation
        ├── ubMinBloodcats
        └── ubMaxBloodcats
```

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `SectorGrid` identifies a sector whose names and terrain are defined in [SectorNames](SectorNames.md); the difficulty sections mirror the campaign difficulty levels (`NOVICE` = 0, `EXPERIENCED` = 1, `EXPERT` = 2, `INSANE` = 3).
- `ubPlacementType` is difficulty-independent: it is stored once per sector.
- `ubMaxBloodcats` is also the sector's bloodcat capacity (`SectorInfo.bBloodCatPlacements`), which clamps the ambush count.
- At game start at least one sector must have placement type `2` (lair), otherwise initialisation throws.
- `ubFactionAffiliation` is only applied to static placement; the values are civilian-group indices shared with [CivGroupNames](../CivGroupNames.md).

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: The table has no display text; sector codes and numeric values are not localized.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: `XML_Bloodcats.cpp` (loader), `Strategic Movement.cpp` (ambush and lair logic), `Game Init.cpp` (initial population and lair requirement), `LOS.cpp` and `Overhead.cpp` (static faction behaviour).
- Map table data.
- Field names and XML comments.
- Descriptions cover the code path that consumes each field; no row counts or observed data ranges are used.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `fRespawn` is stored but not read by 1.13 gameplay code; whether lair replenishment was meant to be optional is not implemented in this source.
- The one-point-per-hour ramp of `ubAmbushChance` since the sector was last loaded is code-defined and not documented by the table.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Cities.xml` defines the towns of Arulco, the country name and the sector-to-town matrix. The
game reads it at the start of a new campaign; the values drive town loyalty, rebel sentiment,
militia permission, strategic-map icons and the town name shown for a sector.

The file is not a single flat list: it contains one `COUNTRY` singleton, a `CITYLIST` of
towns, and a `CITY_TABLE` sector-to-town matrix.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Cities` | `Map/Cities.xml` | plus `COUNTRY` and `CITY_TABLE` |

The editor treats `CITYLIST/CITY` as the record collection (key `uiIndex`) and `COUNTRY` as a
root singleton. `CITY_TABLE` is a special matrix, not a record collection.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
CITY_INFO
├── CITYLIST
│   └── CITY
│       ├── uiIndex
│       ├── townName
│       ├── townUsesLoyalty
│       ├── townRebelSentiment
│       ├── townMilitiaAllowed
│       ├── hiddenTown
│       ├── townIcon
│       ├── szIconFile
│       ├── iconPosition
│       │   ├── x
│       │   └── y
│       ├── baseSector
│       │   ├── x
│       │   └── y
│       └── townPoint
│           ├── x
│           └── y
├── COUNTRY
│   ├── countryName
│   └── countryNoun
└── CITY_TABLE
    └── CITY_TABLE_ROW
```

`uiIndex` is the town array index. The loader ignores `0` (reserved for "no town") and values
outside the array; the highest valid index + 1 becomes `NUM_TOWNS`. Duplicate indexes would
overwrite earlier rows.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `CITY_INFO/CITY_TABLE/CITY_TABLE_ROW` cells -> `CITY_INFO/CITYLIST/CITY/uiIndex`.
- [Facilities](Facilities.md) places facilities in sectors; facility names come from
  [FacilityTypes](FacilityTypes.md).
- `townName`, `countryName` and `countryNoun` are the only translatable fields; see
  `../../Localization.md`.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
`Map/Russian.Cities.xml` is the v4 overlay. It contains `countryName`, `countryNoun` and
`townName` only, keyed by `uiIndex`. Numeric fields, the `CITY_TABLE` matrix and the icon
fields stay in the base file.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
v4 and v5 have the same fields and structure. v4 ships the Russian overlay; v5 has no
`Russian.*` file, which is normal for the English base.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: the strategic-map loader, validation and map UI.
- Table data: `Map/Cities.xml` and `Map/Russian.Cities.xml`.
- `hiddenTown` is a known naming trap: the XML value is correct, but the internal visibility
  flag is inverted. This is described in the field entry above.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `townPoint` is described by the XML comment as tenths of a sector; the loader stores the
  parsed integer, and the exact scaling to screen pixels is in the map UI, not in this table.
- `hiddenTown` is correct per the XML comment, but the internal flag is inverted. Do not use
  the internal flag name as the meaning of the XML field.
- The matrix dimensions are fixed by the code. A total-conversion mod with a different
  world size would need a code change, not only XML edits.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`CreaturePlacements.xml` has two parts. `COMPOSITION_LIST` defines colony compositions and their population caps; `PLACEMENT_LIST` defines an attack source, alternate map, warp destination, queen sector and habitat sectors for each creature infestation. Habitats reference a composition by `CompIndex`.

Within each composition the six `*Percent` fields are consecutive bands of a `Random(100)` roll, processed in the order Larvae, Infant, YoungMale, YoungFemale, AdultMale, AdultFemale; they must add up to exactly `100`. Placement `Index` values are 1-based, composition `CompIndex` values are 0-based, and a habitat whose `Composition` is `0` is ignored.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `GetWarpOutOfMineCodes` itself only rejects `z == 0`; the `z >= 2` and quest-complete checks live in its callers, so a future caller could warp at level 1.
- The loader's `Index` guard accepts `11` and its `CompIndex` guard accepts `50`, one past the end of the corresponding arrays; whether this is intentional is unknown.
- Omitted placement scalars and composition percentages inherit the previous record's value because the parse scratch structs are not cleared per record; whether the game relies on this is unknown.
- Whether `MaxPopulation` is also bounded by `MAX_NUMBER_CREATURES_IN_TACTICAL` in every spreading path is not fully traced here.

tables/Map/Facilities.md.title: Facilities - facility placement
tables/Map/Facilities.md.summary: Facilities.xml places facility instances on the strategic map. Each record says which facility type is present in a sector and how it is revealed in the sector popup. The facility type itself (name, assignment, effects) is defined in FacilityTypes; this table only binds a type to a sector.

SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/FacilityType.description: Index of the facility type in FacilityTypes.ubIndex. It selects the facility's name, assignment, staff limits and effects.
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/FacilityType.values: 0 means "no facility" and the loader skips the record; non-zero values are valid FacilityTypes.ubIndex IDs.
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/FacilityType.source: game code (facility placement loader); facility type data.

SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/SectorGrid.description: Sector where the facility is placed, for example B13. The loader takes the first character as the map row (A..P) and the remaining text as the column (1..16).
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/SectorGrid.values: A1..P16; the loader accepts only rows/columns 1..16 and ignores an invalid sector.
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/SectorGrid.default: none; an invalid value leaves the record unplaced.
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/SectorGrid.source: game code (facility placement loader); facility type data.

SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/ubHidden.description: When the facility appears in the sector info popup: always, after the sector has been explored, or never. 2 is a valid value, so do not treat this as a plain 0/1 flag.
SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY/ubHidden.source: game code (facility placement loader); facility type data.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Facilities.xml` places facility instances on the strategic map. Each record says which
facility type is present in a sector and how it is revealed in the sector popup. The facility
type itself (name, assignment, effects) is defined in `FacilityTypes`; this table only
binds a type to a sector.

sections.heading: Tables
sections.text:
| Table | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Facilities` | `Map/Facilities.xml` | no metadata key; the logical key is sector + type |

`Facilities` has no row in the editor metadata, so the editor shows it as a
document-driven table.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.text:
```
SECTORFACILITIES
└── FACILITY
    ├── SectorGrid
    ├── FacilityType
    └── ubHidden
```

The loader stores the record in `gFacilityLocations[sector][facilityType]`. The logical key is
the pair `SectorGrid + FacilityType`; the file itself has no key element. A duplicate pair
would overwrite the previous flags (last record wins).

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `Facilities.FacilityType` -> [FacilityTypes](FacilityTypes.md) `ubIndex`.
- The sector code determines which town/region the facility belongs to; town data is in
  [Cities](Cities.md).
- Facility names, tooltips and assignment text live in [FacilityTypes](FacilityTypes.md) and its
  `Russian.*` overlay, not in this table.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
No strings in this table. The visible facility name and assignment text come from
`FacilityTypes`; see `Localization.md` for the overlay rules.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
v4 and v5 use the same three fields and the same `SECTORFACILITIES/FACILITY` structure. The
placed facilities may differ; compare the files when a specific sector matters.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: the facility placement loader and the facility type loader.
- Table data: `Map/Facilities.xml`; its header comment documents the three fields.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- There is no metadata key row for `Facilities`; the composite key is a logical contract
  used by the editor, not a declared `TableKeys` entry. Adding a key would be a metadata task,
  not a data edit.
- The parser stores `ubHidden` in a byte-like flag; the value 2 survives, but the internal
  type name is misleading.

tables/Map/FacilityTypes.md.title: FacilityTypes - facilities, assignments and production lines
tables/Map/FacilityTypes.md.summary: FacilityTypes.xml defines facility types and the assignments that can be performed there. A facility has a name, staff limits and optional PMC entry point; each assignment has a type, tooltip, staff limit, performance, cost, fatigue/sleep values and optional morale, loyalty, drunkenness and injury effects. Facilities can also define production lines that turn inputs into items at an hourly cost and loyalty requirement.

FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.description: Base result of the drunkenness event. The current code only tests whether the final result is non-zero, then applies one of the listed drugitem entries, or alcohol when the list is empty.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.numericSemantics: A non-zero result enables the event; the sign and magnitude of the value do not change the effect.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8.

FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.description: Item ID of a drug or drink that can be consumed when the drunk event fires. The element may repeat, and the game picks one entry at random, so repeating an ID makes it more likely rather than adding a quantity.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.values: -32768..32767; the loader stores each entry as INT16.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.default: Empty list; the game then applies alcohol.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.source: game code (facility type loader drug-item vector; facility risk result); map table data.

FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.description: Chance per hour that a mercenary gets drunk on this assignment, expressed against the INI setting FACILITY_EVENT_RARITY (default 1000). As with every ubChance, the loader takes the written value modulo 256.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.numericSemantics: Higher values are more likely; 0 disables the effect, and negative values wrap into the large end of the byte range.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.values: Intended 0..1000; effective stored range 0..255 because of the loader cast.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.source: game code (facility type loader (UINT8) cast; facility risk roll); map table data.

FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.description: Random deviation added around the base drunkenness result.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.numericSemantics: Higher values mean more variation; negative values are not meaningful.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/DR.source: game code (facility type loader; facility risk result); map table data.

FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/IN.numericSemantics: More negative base values cause more damage; a positive base value does not heal, and 0 can still produce damage through ubRange.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/IN.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8.
FACILITYTYPES/FACILITYTYPE/ASSIGNMENT/IN.source: game code (facility type loader; facility risk result); map table data.

The loader stores the value in one byte, so a written value is taken modulo 256: 500 is stored as 244, and only values up to 255 behave as their face value.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`FacilityTypes.xml` defines facility types and the assignments that can be performed there. A facility has a name, staff limits and optional PMC entry point; each assignment has a type, tooltip, staff limit, performance, cost, fatigue/sleep values and optional morale, loyalty, drunkenness and injury effects. Facilities can also define production lines that turn inputs into items at an hourly cost and loyalty requirement.

Risk chances are expressed against the INI setting `FACILITY_EVENT_RARITY` (default `1000`, so a stored `250` is about 25% per hour). The loader stores every `ubChance` through a one-byte cast, so written values are taken modulo 256: `500` becomes `244`, not 50%. The shipped `usChance` element is not on the loader's element list at all, and `usPerformance` nested inside `CONDITIONS` is skipped for the same reason.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The loader stores `ubChance` in one byte, so the intended `0..1000` scale cannot be used for values above `255`; a shipped `500` is meant as 50% on that scale but is actually stored as `244`. The shipped `usChance` value `700` is not read at all. Whether these values were authored for a loader that honoured the full scale is unknown.
- `usChance` has no loader case and no effect; whether it is a leftover of an older schema or a planned alternative is unknown.
- `usPerformance` inside `CONDITIONS` is skipped by the loader; whether the shipped values were expected to apply is unknown.

tables/Map/InteractiveActions.md.title: InteractiveActions - interactive tile actions
tables/Map/InteractiveActions.md.summary: InteractiveActions.xml binds tilesets and structure indexes to an action type, difficulty, optional sector/level restrictions and an optional Lua action. Repeated usTileIndex elements widen one action to several structures; for a sector-specific row, repeated sStructureGridno elements widen it to several exact locations.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/SectorGrid.description: Sector restriction, written as a row letter followed by a column number (A1..P16). The loader converts it to a sector ID and keeps it only when the row and column are both 1..16; matching also requires sectorlevel to equal the current sector level.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/SectorGrid.numericSemantics: The first character is the row (masked with 0x1F, so lower case also works) and the remaining characters are the decimal column. An absent or invalid value leaves the default sector -1, which means no sector restriction.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/SectorGrid.default: Absent or invalid = -1 (any sector); an empty element also leaves -1.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/SectorGrid.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; sector matching); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/difficulty.description: Difficulty threshold compared with the acting soldier's interactive-action skill. The skill is derived from the action type (hacking background skill, wisdom, or a fixed value such as 100) and is normally on a 0..100 scale. The default action succeeds when the skill is at least this value; the multi-turn hacking completion path passes skill > difficulty to the default result.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/difficulty.numericSemantics: Higher values mean harder. The loader stores the value without clamping or rejecting it; because the skill is unsigned and the comparison widens to INT32, a negative difficulty makes the check trivially true.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/difficulty.default: 0; an empty element is parsed as 0.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/difficulty.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; interactive-action skill check and default result); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/luaactionid.description: Lua action ID. When it is >= 0, the game calls the Lua interactive-action result handler (HandleInteractiveActionResult) with this ID; -1 means no Lua call and the fixed default result is used.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/luaactionid.values: -1 disables the Lua call; 0..2147483647 is the ID passed to Lua.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/luaactionid.default: -1; an empty element is parsed as 0, which requests a Lua call with ID 0.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/luaactionid.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; interactive-action result dispatch); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sActionType.description: Action type code used by the interaction system: 0 no action, 1 hack a computer, 2 read a file, 3 take water, 4 buy soda, 5 play a minigame, 6 various.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sActionType.values: 0..6 have defined behaviour; the loader stores the value as UINT16 without range validation.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sActionType.default: 0 (no action); an empty element is parsed as 0.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sActionType.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; INTERACTIVE_STRUCTURE_TYPE enum); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sLevel.description: Map level used with sStructureGridno to refine an exact-location match for a sector-specific action: 0 floor, 1 roof, -1 don't care. The loader clamps the value to 0..1 when the element is present. For an anywhere row the game ignores it.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sLevel.default: -1 (don't care); an empty element is parsed as 0 (floor).
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sLevel.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; structure matching); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sStructureGrid.description: Exact structure grid number (the structure's base grid) for a sector-specific action. The element may repeat, and any matching entry applies. It is consulted only when SectorGrid and sectorlevel are set; for an anywhere row the game ignores it.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sStructureGrid.values: Grid number; the loader stores this field as INT32. The element may repeat.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sStructureGrid.default: Empty list when omitted; an empty element adds grid number 0.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sStructureGrid.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; structure matching); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sectorlevel.description: Sector level for the restriction: 0 surface, 1..3 basement, -1 any. The loader clamps the value to -1..3. A sector-specific row matches only when this equals the current sector level, so a row with -1 behaves as an anywhere row only when SectorGrid is also absent.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sectorlevel.default: -1 (any); an empty element is parsed as 0 (surface).
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/sectorlevel.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; sector matching); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/szTileSetName.description: Tileset file that contains the interactive structure, for example o_furn.sti. It is matched case-insensitively against the tileset's tile-surface file names, comparing the first 11 characters.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/szTileSetName.values: Free text; stored in a 20-byte buffer without appending a terminator, so longer text is truncated and may fill the buffer.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/szTileSetName.default: Empty when omitted; an empty name matches no tileset.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/szTileSetName.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; tileset matching); table data and XML comment.

INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/usTileIndex.description: Structure index within szTileSetName that triggers this action; the game compares it with the structure's usStructureNumber. The element may repeat, and any matching entry applies.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/usTileIndex.values: 0..65535; the loader stores this field as UINT16. The element may repeat.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/usTileIndex.default: Empty list when omitted (the row matches no structure); an empty element adds index 0.
INTERACTIVEACTIONS/ACTION/usTileIndex.source: game code (interactive-actions loader; structure matching); table data and XML comment.

tables/Map/SamSites.md.title: SamSites - SAM sites and covered sectors
tables/Map/SamSites.md.summary: SamSites.xml defines SAM installations and the matrix of sectors they cover. Each SAM has a sector, hidden flag, terminal orientation and two terminal grid positions. The coverage matrix holds one row per map row; each cell is a bitmask of the SAMs covering that sector, not a single SAM index.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoA.description: Grid number of the lower terminal tile on the tactical map (the A tile in the table comment's A/B diagram).
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoA.values: Tactical grid number below MAX_ALLOWED_WORLD_MAX; values at or above it are replaced with 0.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoA.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoB.description: Grid number of the upper terminal tile (the B tile); samGridNoA is always lower on screen than samGridNoB.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoB.values: Tactical grid number below MAX_ALLOWED_WORLD_MAX; values at or above it are replaced with 1.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samGridNoB.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samHidden.description: If nonzero, the SAM site is hidden at the start of a new game (fSamSiteFoundOrig is set to !samHidden). Changing it in an existing save has no effect; the table comment requires a new game.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samHidden.values: 0 or 1; any nonzero value hides the site.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samHidden.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samIndex.description: Unique 1-based SAM-site index used as the array key (stored internally at samIndex - 1). NUMBER_OF_SAMS is set to the highest index read; indices 1..4 also have hardcoded Meanwhile/Skyrider roles.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samIndex.values: 1..50 (MAX_NUMBER_OF_SAMS); 0 is reserved for 'no SAM coverage' and is rejected as a site index.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samIndex.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samOrientation.description: Orientation of the SAM control terminal if it is repaired: 3 for / (from the middle to the lower left) and 4 for \ (from the middle to the lower right). Any other value is forced to 3.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samOrientation.values: 3 or 4; other values are read as 3.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samOrientation.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samSector/x.description: Map column (x) of the SAM sector: 1 = west edge, 16 = east edge. Used with y to build the sector ID.
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samSector/x.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samSector/y.description: Map row (y) of the SAM sector: 1 = north edge (A), 16 = south edge (P).
SAM_INFO/SAMLIST/SAM/samSector/y.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

SAM_INFO/SAM_CONTROLLED_SECTORS/MAP_ROW.description: One row of the SAM coverage matrix. The row attribute selects the map row (00..17); the element text is a whitespace-separated list of 18 column cells. Each cell is a bitmask: bit 0 = SAM 1, bit 1 = SAM 2, bit 2 = SAM 3, and so on, so 5 means SAM 1 and SAM 3; 0 = no coverage.
SAM_INFO/SAM_CONTROLLED_SECTORS/MAP_ROW.values: 18 cells, one per column 0..17; rows and columns 0 and 17 are world borders and are not read by the coverage checks.
SAM_INFO/SAM_CONTROLLED_SECTORS/MAP_ROW.default: Required; rows with a missing row attribute or row >= 18 are skipped. A non-numeric value is parsed as 0.
SAM_INFO/SAM_CONTROLLED_SECTORS/MAP_ROW.source: game code (SAM-site loader and coverage code); table data and XML comments.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The coverage matrix is a bitmask (`1 << (samIndex - 1)`), not a list of SAM indexes; shipped values include combinations such as `5`, `6`, `9`, `12` and `13`.
- `samIndex` 1..4 have hardcoded roles in the Meanwhile/Skyrider dialogue and retreat logic; changing them can break those scenes.
- The loader stores matrix rows/columns `0` and `17` even though the coverage checks only read `1..16`; whether a non-zero border value has any effect is unknown.
- The matrix parser has no column-count check; a row with more than 18 cells would write past the row array.

tables/Map/SectorLoadscreens.md.title: SectorLoadscreens - sector loading screens
tables/Map/SectorLoadscreens.md.summary: SectorLoadscreens.xml maps a sector to the image shown while it loads. Record 0 is the landing-zone/helicopter screen; records 1..256 are matched by szLocation against the current surface sector. Images are extensionless paths under the game data directory: the loader appends a resolution suffix and probes .png then .sti. A missing or empty path does not fall back to a generic screen; the game fills the screen black and prints a "loadscreen data file not found" message. The loader also parses alternate day/night fields, but the current display code uses only the day alternate.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/RandomAltSector.description: If set, the game makes a 50/50 choice between the primary and alternate screens for day or night (Random(2) > 0). With the current display code only the day alternate is effective (see szNightAlt).
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/RandomAltSector.values: 0 or 1; any nonzero value is treated as set.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/RandomAltSector.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDay.description: Path to the primary daytime loading-screen image, relative to the game data directory and without an extension (for example Loadscreens\LS_DayTropical). The loader appends a resolution suffix and probes .png then .sti.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDay.values: Free text path up to 79 characters (CHAR8[80]); empty = no daytime image (the display then reports a missing file).
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDay.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDayAlt.description: Path to the alternate daytime loading-screen image, used when RandomAltSector picks the alternate and the screen is DAY. Same extensionless-path rules as szDay.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDayAlt.values: Free text path up to 79 characters; empty = no alternate day image (the display then reports a missing file instead of falling back to szDay).
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szDayAlt.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szImageFormat.description: Image-format label from the table (STI or PNG in shipped data). The current surface-sector selection does not read it; it probes .png and .sti filenames itself, so this field does not choose the file extension.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szImageFormat.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szImageFormatAlt.description: Alternate image-format label; when RandomAltSector picks the alternate and this value is non-empty, it replaces szImageFormat. Like szImageFormat, it is not used to choose the surface file extension in the current code.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szImageFormatAlt.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szLocation.description: Sector code (A1..P16) whose loading screen this record supplies, or START for the landing zone in record 0. Records 1..256 are matched against the current sector code; record 0 is read directly for the helicopter screen.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szLocation.values: A1..P16 or START; stored in a CHAR8[10] buffer.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szLocation.default: Required for records 1..256; record 0 uses the landing-zone screen regardless of its text.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szLocation.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNight.description: Path to the primary nighttime loading-screen image, relative to the game data directory and without an extension. Same resolution-suffix and .png/.sti probing as szDay.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNight.values: Free text path up to 79 characters (CHAR8[80]); empty = no nighttime image (the display then reports a missing file).
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNight.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNightAlt.description: Path to the alternate nighttime loading-screen image in the table, but the current DisplayLoadScreenWithID uses szNight for the NIGHT_ALT case, so this value is parsed and never read by the display code. The shipped B2 record, for example, keeps LS_NightChitzena instead of LS_MineNight.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNightAlt.values: Free text path up to 79 characters; ignored by the current display code.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/szNightAlt.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/uiIndex.description: Index of the loading-screen record and the array slot it is stored in; it must be unique. Record 0 is used directly for the helicopter/landing-zone screen.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/uiIndex.values: 0..256 (MAX_SECTOR_LOADSCREENS - 1); the loader parses decimal or 0x hexadecimal and drops records outside the range.
LOADSCREENS/SECTOR/uiIndex.source: game code (sector-loadscreens loader and display); table data and XML comments.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: `SectorLoadscreens.xml` maps a sector to the image shown while it loads. Record `0` is the landing-zone/helicopter screen; records `1..256` are matched by `szLocation` against the current surface sector. Images are extensionless paths under the game data directory: the loader appends a resolution suffix and probes `.png` then `.sti`. A missing or empty path does not fall back to a generic screen; the game fills the screen black and prints a "loadscreen data file not found" message. The loader also parses alternate day/night fields, but the current display code uses only the day alternate.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `DisplayLoadScreenWithID` selects `szNight` for the `NIGHT_ALT` case instead of `szNightAlt`, so `szNightAlt` is parsed but never used; whether this is a bug or intended is unknown.

- If no record matches, or the selected path is empty or missing, the game shows a black screen with a diagnostic; whether a generic fallback was intended is unknown.

tables/Map/SectorNames.md.title: SectorNames - sector names, weather and population
tables/Map/SectorNames.md.summary: SectorNames.xml gives each map sector its explored and unexplored names, weather and snake chances, water and dirt values, civilian population, wealth, curfew, prison room and raid switches. The table is keyed by SectorGrid.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/SectorGrid.description: Sector code in A1..P16 form: the letter is the map row (y) and the number is the column (x). It is the table key.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/SectorGrid.values: A1..P16; both coordinates must be 1..16, otherwise the parser keeps its previous coordinates.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/SectorGrid.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/banditraidpossible.description: If nonzero, bandits can raid this sector; the loader sets SECTORFLAG_RAIDPOSSIBLE_BANDIT in the level-0 sector flag mask.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/banditraidpossible.values: 0 or 1; any nonzero value sets the flag.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/banditraidpossible.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/bloodcatraidpossible.description: If nonzero, bloodcats can raid this sector; the loader sets SECTORFLAG_RAIDPOSSIBLE_BLOODCAT in the level-0 sector flag mask.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/bloodcatraidpossible.values: 0 or 1; any nonzero value sets the flag.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/bloodcatraidpossible.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/maxworkers.description: Maximum number of workers that can be employed in this sector. Used as the town-worker cap and to seed the initial workforce (maxworkers dInitialWorkerRate).
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/maxworkers.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/numsnakes.description: Maximum number of snakes for a snake attack. A positive attack creates 1 + Random(numsnakes) snakes, so the actual count is 1..numsnakes.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/numsnakes.values: 0..20; the loader caps at 20 even though the table comment says 0..100.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/numsnakes.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/rainchance.description: Per-sector weather weight used when localizing rain: it biases the starting sector and is the chance that an adjacent sector also gets the weather. It is not a standalone daily rain probability.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/rainchance.values: 0..100; the loader stores UINT8 and applies min(100, value) after the cast.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/rainchance.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sRadioScanModifier.description: Additive modifier to the radio-scan assignment range in this sector; the base range is the RADIO_OPERATOR_ASSIGNMENT_SCAN_BASE_RANGE setting in Ja2_Options.ini (default 5) and the result must be at least 1 for the scan to run.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sRadioScanModifier.numericSemantics: positive = longer range, negative = shorter range. The loader clamps values above 3 to 3; the intended -3 lower clamp is overwritten in the current source, so lower negative values are kept.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sRadioScanModifier.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sWaterType.description: Water category: 0 = no water, 1 = drinkable water, 2 = salt water, 3 = water that may pose a health risk (poisoned or swamp water).
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sWaterType.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sandstormchance.description: Per-sector weather weight used when localizing sandstorms: it biases the starting sector and is the chance that an adjacent sector also gets the weather. It is not a standalone daily sandstorm probability.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sandstormchance.values: 0..100; the loader stores UINT8 and applies min(100, value) after the cast.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/sandstormchance.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snakechance.description: Per-turn chance, in percent, that snakes can attack people in water in this sector; evaluated only on the surface (z = 0) when snakes are enabled.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snakechance.values: 0..100; the loader stores UINT8 and caps at 100 after the cast.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snakechance.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snowchance.description: Per-sector weather weight used when localizing snow: it biases the starting sector and is the chance that an adjacent sector also gets the weather. It is not a standalone daily snow probability.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snowchance.values: 0..100; the loader stores UINT8 and applies min(100, value) after the cast.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/snowchance.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedExploredNa.description: Detailed explored-sector name; stored in slot 3 and used in the detailed name after the sector is visited or a SAM site there is known.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedExploredNa.default: Absent; empty string. All four name fields must be non-empty or the whole custom set is ignored.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedExploredNa.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedUnexplored.description: Detailed unexplored-sector name; stored in slot 1 and used in the detailed strategic-map sector name.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedUnexplored.default: Absent; empty string. All four name fields must be non-empty or the whole custom set is ignored.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szDetailedUnexplored.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szExploredName.description: Short explored-sector name; stored in slot 2 and used in the non-detailed name after the sector is visited or a SAM site there is known.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szExploredName.default: Absent; empty string. All four name fields must be non-empty or the whole custom set is ignored.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szExploredName.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/szUnexploredName.description: Short unexplored-sector name; stored in slot 0 and used in the non-detailed strategic-map sector name.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/usCurfewValue.description: Curfew category used for covert-civilian detection: 0 = no curfew, 1 = night curfew, 2 = civilians never allowed. The tactical AI raises the effective value to at least 1 at night and to at least 2 underground.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/usCurfewValue.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/usNaturalDirt.description: Dirt-accumulation percentage for guns fired in a surface sector: 100 is a clean city, and higher values accumulate dirt proportionally faster (1000 = desert, ten times faster). The firing code multiplies the item's dirt factor by this value and divides by 5000, with a minimum factor of 1; being indoors halves the value, and underground sectors use a fixed 100.
