SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/usPrisonRoomNumber.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/wealth.description: Rating of how rich the sector's population is; also used as the money scale for scrounging (wealth + Random(4 wealth)), so 0 disables that behaviour.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/wealth.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/zombieraidpossible.description: If nonzero, zombies can raid this sector; the loader sets SECTORFLAG_RAIDPOSSIBLE_ZOMBIE in the level-0 sector flag mask.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/zombieraidpossible.values: 0 or 1; any nonzero value sets the flag.
SECTOR_NAMES/SECTOR/zombieraidpossible.source: game code (sector-names loader and related game systems); table data and XML comments.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`SectorNames.xml` gives each map sector its explored and unexplored names, weather and snake chances, water and dirt values, civilian population, wealth, curfew, prison room and raid switches. The table is keyed by `SectorGrid`.

All four `sz*Name` fields must be non-empty for a sector's custom names to be used; if any one is empty, the game ignores the custom set and generates default names for all four. `rainchance`, `sandstormchance` and `snowchance` are per-sector weights in localized weather, not standalone daily probabilities.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `SectorNames.SectorGrid` is the canonical sector key used by [SectorLoadscreens](SectorLoadscreens.md), [MovementCosts](MovementCosts.md), [BloodcatPlacements](BloodcatPlacements.md) and [CreaturePlacements](CreaturePlacements.md).
- The row's `SectorGrid` is parsed as a letter (row `y`) followed by a number (column `x`); the resulting sector ID keys the name and external-data arrays.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Game code: sector-names loader; weather, dirt, disease, worker, radio-scan, prison-room and curfew systems.
- Map table data and XML comments.
- Field types follow the runtime sector-data structure and loader casts; descriptions follow the code that consumes each value.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- The loader computes `max(-3, value)` and then immediately overwrites it with `min(3, value)`, so the intended `-3` lower clamp is not applied; whether this is intended is unknown.
- An invalid or missing `SectorGrid` is not rejected: the parser reuses the previous record's coordinates (or `0,0` for the first record), and the record can overwrite another sector. Whether the loader should reject it is unknown.
- `rainchance`, `sandstormchance` and `snowchance` feed `DetermineLocalizedWeatherGivenHelperArray`, which uses them both to pick a starting sector and to spread weather to adjacent sectors; the full localization formula is not described here.
- Prison rooms and raid flags are written to the level-0 (`[0]`) runtime slot only; the level-1..3 slots are left at zero, and whether the level files are meant to define them is unknown.
- The loader resets `usNaturalDirt` to `100` after each record, so an omitted value in the first record starts from `0` while later records start from `100`; whether that asymmetry is intended is unknown.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- `uiIndex` is referenced by `Inventory.MercStartingGear.mIndex`, `MercOpinions.uiIndex`, `MercQuote.uiIndex`, `MercAvailability.ProfilId` and `AIMAvailability.ProfilId`.
- `usBackground` points to [Backgrounds](Backgrounds.md); `ubCivilianGroup` points to [CivGroupNames](CivGroupNames.md).
- `ubFaceIndex` points to [RPCFacesSmall](RPCFacesSmall.md); `usVoiceIndex` points to [IMPVoices](IMPVoices.md).
- `bTown` and town-related fields use the town indexes in [Cities](Map/Cities.md).

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: `zName`, `zNickname` and the palette keys are display/presentation data. Numeric stats, traits and IDs are not localized.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Merc profile table data.
- MercProfiles schema comments.
- Game code: profile XML loader, profile struct and loader, soldier creation, campaign growth, face renderer, strategic merc handler, strategic status.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text: The full nationality list is maintained in the table schema comment; it is not repeated here. The growth-modifier tags are spelled `GrowthModifier*` in the table, while the loader in the analyzed source revision matches `bGrowthModifier*`, so whether the shipped build reads these values is unresolved.

tables/MercStartingGear.md.title: MercStartingGear - starting equipment kits
tables/MercStartingGear.md.summary: MercStartingGear.xml defines each mercenary’s starting equipment. A mercenary can have up to five named GEARKIT blocks (NUM_MERCSTARTINGGEAR_KITS); each block lists the items, condition, quantity and drop flags for the kit.

MERCGEARLIST/MERCGEAR/GEARKIT/lBPack.description: Item ID in the NIV backpack LBE slot (BPACKPOCKPOS).
MERCGEARLIST/MERCGEAR/GEARKIT/lBPack.default: 0 when omitted; an empty element follows the game default.
MERCGEARLIST/MERCGEAR/GEARKIT/lBPack.source: game code (starting-gear loader); merc starting-gear table data.

MERCGEARLIST/MERCGEAR/GEARKIT/lBPackStat.description: Condition of the NIV backpack LBE item (percent; 100 = new).
MERCGEARLIST/MERCGEAR/GEARKIT/lBPackStat.numericSemantics: Percentage; higher values mean better condition. The value is passed to the item's objectStatus when the soldier is created; LBE stack size is always 1.

tables/NPCInventory/Traders.md.title: Traders - merchants and dealer inventories
tables/NPCInventory/Traders.md.summary: Merchants.xml defines dealer identity, cash, buy/sell multipliers, coolness progression, daily restock, delivery delays and availability flags. Each Inventory.xml file lists the items and target quantities for one dealer. The 80 dealer inventories are bound to dealers in the game's initialisation code, by one fixed filename per ARMS_DEALER_ value plus AdditionalDealer_N for the additional dealers, so a file's dealer follows from its name and not from any value inside it. Slots 0..19 are the named shopkeepers in enum order and slots 20..79 are the additional-dealer slots used by town shops and generic dealers; the shipped table fills slots up to 68, and the array is zero-filled, so the remaining slots keep zero merchant data.

INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/sItemIndex.type: Integer (INT16) — the loader stores this field as INT16.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/sItemIndex.description: Item ID stocked by the dealer. 0 is the list terminator (LAST_DEALER_ITEM), so the game stops reading at the first row whose sItemIndex is 0; rows stored in higher slots than that first zero are never seen.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/sItemIndex.values: Item IDs; 0 ends the list and is also the “no item” value.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/sItemIndex.default: 0 when omitted, which ends the list at that row.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/sItemIndex.source: game code (the inventory loader; the inventory lookup).

INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/ubOptimalNumber.type: Integer (UINT8) — the loader stores this field as UINT8.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/ubOptimalNumber.description: Number of the item the dealer aims to keep; the game calls the lookup GetMaxItemAmount and uses it as the initial and maximum supply for the item.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/ubOptimalNumber.numericSemantics: 0 = no stock. The lookup returns the value through an INT8, so a value in 128..255 comes back negative and fails the game's > 0 stock checks; keep the value at 127 or below.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/ubOptimalNumber.source: game code (the inventory loader; the inventory lookup and its callers).

INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/uiIndex.type: Integer (UINT32) — the loader stores this field as UINT32.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/uiIndex.description: Slot of the row in the dealer's inventory array. The game scans that array in slot order, so this is the row's position, not just a label.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/uiIndex.values: 0..16000 (uiIndex < MAXITEMS, and MAXITEMS is 16001); a row with a larger index is silently dropped.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/uiIndex.default: 0 when omitted, so a row without an index overwrites slot 0.
INVENTORYLIST/INVENTORY/uiIndex.source: game code (the inventory loader; the item-count constant).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/addToCoolness.description: Flat amount added to both ends of the merchant's computed coolness range, together with the Rebel Command merchant bonus.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/addToCoolness.numericSemantics: Higher = better stock sooner. The Merchants.xml loader stores any UINT32 without a range check; the 0..10 limit is applied only to <COOLADD> in the legacy CONTROL block of Inventory.xml.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/addToCoolness.values: 0..10 by intent; the shipped table uses 0 and 1.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/addToCoolness.source: game code (the merchant loader; the coolness calculation; the inventory loader for the legacy check).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/allInventoryAlway.description: If set, every item counts as fully suitable for this dealer (ITEM_SUITABILITY_HIGH) regardless of coolness or player progress, so the whole catalogue is available instead of being gated by progression. Bobby Ray's is exempt from this shortcut.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/allInventoryAlway.numericSemantics: A switch: any non-zero value is true.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/allInventoryAlway.source: game code (the merchant loader; the suitability check).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/coolnessProgressR.description: Percentage of the player's progress that sets the merchant's stock coolness. The game computes min = progress rate / 100 and max = min + 1, adds addToCoolness (plus the Rebel Command bonus) to both, bounds the minimum by minCoolness and 9, and bounds the maximum by maxCoolness with a forced max >= min + 1.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/coolnessProgressR.numericSemantics: Percent; higher = faster progression. The Merchants.xml loader applies no range check — the 0..100 check belongs to <PROGRESSRATE> in the legacy CONTROL block — so a value above 100 pushes coolness past the player's progress range.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/coolnessProgressR.default: 0 when omitted, which makes both ends depend only on addToCoolness.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/coolnessProgressR.source: game code (the coolness formula; the merchant loader; the inventory loader for the legacy check).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dBuyModifier.type: Decimal (FLOAT) — a 32-bit float in game code.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dBuyModifier.description: Multiplier applied when the merchant buys from the player; 0.75 pays 75% of value and 1.0 pays full value. For a repair dealer (ubTypeOfArmsDealer 3) the same storage holds dRepairSpeed and scales repair time instead.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dBuyModifier.numericSemantics: The loader clamps the value to 0.1..5.0 (min(5.0f, max(0.1f, value))), so an out-of-range entry is pulled to the nearest bound rather than rejected. Higher = better price for the player.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dBuyModifier.default: 0 when omitted — outside the clamped range, so a merchant without this element would pay nothing; write it explicitly.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dBuyModifier.source: game code (the merchant loader; the dealer-structure union).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dSellModifier.type: Decimal (FLOAT) — a 32-bit float in game code.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dSellModifier.description: Multiplier applied when the merchant sells to the player; 1.25 charges 125% of value and 1.0 charges full value. For a repair dealer (ubTypeOfArmsDealer 3) the same storage holds dRepairCost and scales the price charged for repairs.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dSellModifier.numericSemantics: Clamped by the loader to 0.1..5.0; higher = more expensive.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dSellModifier.default: 0 when omitted — outside the clamped range; write it explicitly.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dSellModifier.source: game code (the merchant loader; the dealer-structure union).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyIncrement.type: Integer (UINT32) — an integer amount, not a decimal.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyIncrement.description: Cash added each day after the retained share: cash = cash dailyRetained / 100 + dailyIncrement, then capped at dailyMaximum.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyIncrement.numericSemantics: Money, in whole units; higher = more daily cash. No clamp in the Merchants.xml loader (the legacy CONTROL block limits <INCREMENT> to 0..1000000).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyIncrement.source: game code (the merchant loader; the daily cash reset).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyMaximum.type: Integer (UINT32) — an integer amount, not a decimal.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyMaximum.description: Ceiling for the cash the merchant accumulates: after the daily update the cash is lowered to this value when it is higher.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyMaximum.numericSemantics: Money; higher = larger cap. A cap of 0 therefore empties the dealer's cash on every daily reset.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyMaximum.default: 0 when omitted, so an omitted value caps the dealer at zero cash.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyMaximum.source: game code (the merchant loader; the daily cash reset).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyRetained.type: Integer (UINT32) — an integer percentage, not a decimal despite the d prefix.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyRetained.description: Share of the current cash the merchant keeps on the daily reset, in percent, before dailyIncrement is added and dailyMaximum is applied.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyRetained.numericSemantics: Percent: 100 keeps everything, 0 keeps nothing. No clamp in the Merchants.xml loader (the legacy CONTROL block limits <RETAINED> to 0..100).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/dailyRetained.source: game code (the merchant loader; the daily cash reset).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMax.type: Integer (UINT32) — whole days, not a decimal.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMax.description: Upper bound of the delivery delay: the game picks daysDelayMin + Random(daysDelayMax - daysDelayMin).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMax.numericSemantics: Days; keep it at or above daysDelayMin, because the difference is computed in unsigned arithmetic and a smaller maximum wraps to a huge random range. No clamp in the Merchants.xml loader (the legacy CONTROL block limits <REORDERMAXIMUM> to 1..10).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMax.source: game code (the merchant loader; the reorder delay).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMin.type: Integer (UINT32) — whole days, not a decimal.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMin.description: Lower bound of the delivery delay for reordered items; the delay is daysDelayMin + Random(daysDelayMax - daysDelayMin) days.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMin.numericSemantics: Days; the structure's comment intends 1..10, but the Merchants.xml loader does not check it (the legacy CONTROL block limits <REORDERMINIMUM> to 1..10).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMin.default: 0 when omitted, which with an omitted maximum yields a 0-day delay.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/daysDelayMin.source: game code (the merchant loader; the reorder delay).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/iInitialCash.description: Cash the merchant starts with. The game also resets a dealer's cash to this amount when the dealer is re-initialised.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/iInitialCash.numericSemantics: Money, in whole units; higher = richer. There is no clamp in the Merchants.xml loader (the legacy CONTROL block limits its <INITIAL> to 0..1000000), and a negative value is stored but not meaningful.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/iInitialCash.default: 0 when omitted, because each record is zero-filled before parsing.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/iInitialCash.source: game code (the merchant loader; the dealer initialisation).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/maxCoolness.description: Upper bound applied to the merchant's computed maximum stock coolness.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/maxCoolness.numericSemantics: Clamped to 1..10 when present, then used as min(maxCoolness, computedMax); the game afterwards forces the maximum to be at least the minimum plus one.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/maxCoolness.default: 0 when omitted, which is below the clamp range and lets the computed maximum stand.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/maxCoolness.source: game code (the merchant loader clamp; the coolness calculation).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/minCoolness.description: Lower bound applied to the merchant's computed minimum stock coolness.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/minCoolness.numericSemantics: The loader clamps a present value to 1..10 (min(10, max(1, value))), although the structure's comment still says 0-10. The value then acts as max(minCoolness, min(9, computedMin)).
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/minCoolness.default: 0 when omitted, which is below the clamp range and leaves the computed minimum unbounded from below.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/minCoolness.source: game code (the merchant loader clamp; the coolness calculation).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/nonprofile_loyalt.description: Town loyalty a non-profile dealer in a city requires before he will trade with the player.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/nonprofile_loyalt.numericSemantics: A loyalty rating, compared against gTownLoyalty[].ubRating; higher = stricter, 0 = no requirement.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/nonprofile_loyalt.source: game code (the merchant loader; the loyalty check).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/szName.description: Informational label for the row, for example Tony or additional dealer 3. The loader reads the element and discards it — the parser branch for szName is marked “not needed, but it's there for informational purposes” — and the structure's comments say the name is “used in xml, not used ingame”. The game shows a shopkeeper's name from the NPC profile.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/szName.values: Free text; it does not reach the game state.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/szName.source: game code (the merchant loader's szName branch and the field comment).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubShopKeeperID.description: NPC profile ID of the shopkeeper, from the NPCIDs enum that the XML comment quotes.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubShopKeeperID.numericSemantics: A profile reference, not an index into this table. The shipped table uses 255 for generic additional dealers and 200 for the town-shop rows.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubShopKeeperID.values: 0..255. The Merchants.xml loader stores the value without a range check; the NUM_PROFILES check exists only in the legacy CONTROL block of Inventory.xml.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubShopKeeperID.source: game code (the merchant loader; the inventory loader for the legacy check); table data.

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubTypeOfArmsDeale.type: Integer (UINT8) — an enum, not a free number.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubTypeOfArmsDeale.description: Dealer behaviour: 0 buys and sells, 1 sells only, 2 buys only, 3 repairs.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubTypeOfArmsDeale.numericSemantics: The loader clamps the value with min(ARMS_DEALER_REPAIRS, value), so only 0..3 survive; a larger value, and also a negative one (it wraps through the UINT8 cast), becomes 3.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubTypeOfArmsDeale.default: 0 when omitted, which means “buys and sells”.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/ubTypeOfArmsDeale.source: game code (the merchant-loader clamp and the dealer-type enum); table XML comment.

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiFlags.description: Packed bitmask of merchant flags. Each bit enables a dealer behaviour.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiFlags.numericSemantics: Bitmask; combine bits with OR. A larger number is not simply “more”. Parsed with a base-0 conversion, so the shipped decimal values and 0x hexadecimal forms are both accepted.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiFlags.values: 0x08000000 only used items, 0x10000000 gives change, 0x20000000 accepts gifts, 0x40000000 some used items, 0x80000000 has no inventory. The dealer structure defines further item-class bits, but Merchants.xml is not where they are normally set.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiFlags.source: game code (the merchant flag constants and the merchant loader); table XML comment.

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiIndex.description: Slot of the merchant in the game's armsDealerInfo array. The loader writes the record to armsDealerInfo[uiIndex], and that slot number is also the ARMS_DEALER_ value that selects the dealer's Inventory.xml file.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiIndex.values: 0..79 (NUM_ARMS_DEALERS is 80); a record with a larger uiIndex is silently dropped.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiIndex.default: 0 when omitted, so a record without an index overwrites slot 0.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/uiIndex.source: game code (the merchant loader; the dealer enum and its count).

MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/useBRSetting.description: If set, the merchant uses Bobby Ray's quality setting for its stock. When ubBobbyRayQuality is better than BR_GOOD, the merchant's maximum coolness is raised by quality - 1, plus one more for used items — the same treatment Bobby Ray's own shop receives.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/useBRSetting.numericSemantics: A switch: the loader parses an integer with atol, so any non-zero value becomes true and 0 becomes false.
MERCHANTSLIST/MERCHANT/useBRSetting.source: game code (the merchant loader; the suitability check).

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text:
`Merchants.xml` defines dealer identity, cash, buy/sell multipliers, coolness progression, daily restock, delivery delays and availability flags. Each `*Inventory.xml` file lists the items and target quantities for one dealer. The 80 dealer inventories are bound to dealers in the game's initialisation code, by one fixed filename per `ARMS_DEALER_*` value plus `AdditionalDealer_N` for the additional dealers, so a file's dealer follows from its name and not from any value inside it. Slots `0..19` are the named shopkeepers in enum order and slots `20..79` are the additional-dealer slots used by town shops and generic dealers; the shipped table fills slots up to `68`, and the array is zero-filled, so the remaining slots keep zero merchant data.

The inventory loader also understands an older `<CONTROL>` block that sets the same merchant fields for the dealer it belongs to. No shipped `*Inventory.xml` contains one; because the inventory files are parsed after `Merchants.xml`, such a block would overwrite that dealer's merchant values.

sections.heading: Relations
sections.text:
- Dealer inventories are separate files, bound to dealers by the fixed filenames in the game's initialisation code; the `Merchants` row at the matching `uiIndex` supplies that dealer's merchant data.
- `sItemIndex` references [Items](../Items/Items.md), and a file's rows are read in `uiIndex` order until `sItemIndex` reaches `0`.
- `ubShopKeeperID` references the NPC profile table; `szName` is informational and is not read by the game.
- A repair dealer (`ubTypeOfArmsDealer` `3`) reuses `dBuyModifier`/`dSellModifier` as repair-speed and repair-price multipliers.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text: Display names and labels are localized through language overlays; numeric IDs and codes are not.

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text: v4 and v5 use the same field paths; values may differ.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
- Table data: `Merchants.xml` and the 80 dealer inventory files.
- Game code: the merchant loader, the inventory loader (including its legacy `CONTROL` block), the dealer structure and flag constants, the daily cash reset, the reorder delay, the coolness and suitability logic, the inventory scan, and the initialisation code that binds each file to a dealer.
- Field names and XML comments, including the `NPCIDs`, `ubTypeOfArmsDealer` and `uiFlags` lists quoted at the top of `Merchants.xml`.
- Every field above cites the code that reads it; no formula is claimed beyond those lines.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.text:
- `uiFlags`: no open question remains — the XML comment lists the five behaviour bits and the dealer structure defines the same constants; the additional item-class bits are usually supplied by the legacy `CONTROL` block.
- Coolness: no open question remains — `min = progress * rate / 100`, `max = min + 1`, `addToCoolness` (plus the Rebel Command merchant bonus) is added to both, the minimum is bounded by `minCoolness` and `9`, and the maximum by `maxCoolness` with a forced `max >= min + 1`.
- Not established here: whether a `<CONTROL>` block in an `*Inventory.xml` is meant to replace `Merchants.xml` for its dealer. The files are parsed after `Merchants.xml`, so such a block would overwrite the dealer's values, but no shipped file contains one.

tables/SpreadPatterns.md.title: SpreadPatterns - shotgun spread patterns
tables/SpreadPatterns.md.summary: SpreadPatterns.xml defines shotgun pellet patterns: explicit pellet angles plus optional random xspread/yspread ranges and a distribution shape. The first pattern is the default when no other is selected.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/DESC.description: Informational description of the pattern. It is not read by the loader and has no runtime effect.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/DESC.values: Free text; ignored at load time.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/NAME.description: Name of the spread pattern, used by other XML files. The name is matched case-insensitively; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed on load.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/NAME.values: Free text; the loader stores at most SPREADPATTERN_NAME_SIZE - 1 characters.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/method.description: Distribution shape for random pellets. The loader matches this value case-sensitively against RECTANGLE, DIAMOND and ELLIPSE; an unmatched value leaves the default ELLIPSE.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/method.numericSemantics: Enum-like text; case and spelling must match the uppercase loader names exactly.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/method.values: RECTANGLE, DIAMOND or ELLIPSE. The XML comment's Rectangle/Diamond/Ellipse spellings do not match and fall back to the default.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/method.source: game code (XML_SpreadPatterns.cpp, LOS.cpp); table XML comment.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/p/x.description: Horizontal angle of one explicit pellet, in radians. Positive values deviate one way, negative the other; it is signed.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/p/x.default: Absent; the pellet entry starts at 0.0.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/p/y.description: Vertical angle of one explicit pellet, in radians. Positive values deviate one way, negative the other; it is signed.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/p/y.default: Absent; the pellet entry starts at 0.0.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/xspread.description: Maximum horizontal random spread, in radians. The loader applies fabs(), so a negative value is stored as its absolute value.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/xspread.numericSemantics: higher = wider spread; 0 disables horizontal randomization.

SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/yspread.description: Maximum vertical random spread, in radians. The loader applies fabs(), so a negative value is stored as its absolute value.
SPREADPATTERNLIST/SPREADPATTERN/yspread.numericSemantics: higher = wider spread; 0 disables vertical randomization.

tables/Vehicles.md.title: Vehicles - vehicle definitions and seats
tables/Vehicles.md.summary: Vehicles.xml defines vehicle names, movement/armour/sound references and the seat layout used when mercenaries ride. Each vehicle can have repeated SEAT entries; this page documents the shared seat field set.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/EnterVehicleSndID.description: Sound ID played when entering the vehicle. It is a sound reference.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/EnterVehicleSndID.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/LongName.description: Long display name shown in detailed UI; may be empty.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/LongName.values: Free text or a symbolic code.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/MoveVehicleSndID.description: Sound ID played when the vehicle moves. It is a sound reference.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/MoveVehicleSndID.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/MvtTypes.description: Movement-type code for the vehicle. It is an enum/bit field.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/MvtTypes.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/Name.values: Free text or a symbolic code.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/Neutral.description: If set, the vehicle is neutral rather than owned by a faction. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/Pilot.description: Profile ID of the default pilot, or -1 when there is no pilot. It is a reference.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/Pilot.values: -128..127; -1 means no pilot. The loader stores this field as INT8.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/BlockedShots.description: If set, shots from this seat are blocked. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/BlockedView.description: If set, the occupant’s view from this seat is blocked. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Compartment.description: Compartment/area code for the seat. It is an enum/reference.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Compartment.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Driver.description: If set, this seat is the driver’s seat. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Hidden.description: If set, the seat/occupant is hidden in the vehicle UI. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetX.description: Horizontal offset of the seat position in pixels.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetX.numericSemantics: increasing = right, decreasing = left; negative values are allowed.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetX.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetY.description: Vertical offset of the seat position in pixels.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetY.numericSemantics: increasing = down, decreasing = up; negative values are allowed.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/OffsetY.values: -128..127; the loader stores this field as INT8.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Rotation.description: Facing/rotation code for the seat occupant. It is an orientation code.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/Rotation.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/SeatIndex.description: Index of the seat within the vehicle. It is a seat key.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/SeatIndex.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/SeatName.description: Display name of the seat, such as Driver or Passenger.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SEAT/SeatName.values: Free text or a symbolic code.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SeatingCapacities.description: Number of seats in the vehicle.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SeatingCapacities.numericSemantics: higher = more seats; negative values are not meaningful.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/SeatingCapacities.values: Integer; see the description for its scale.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/ShortName.description: Short display name for the vehicle; may be empty.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/ShortName.values: Free text or a symbolic code.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/StiFaceIcon.description: STI face icon path for the vehicle. It is a file reference.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/StiFaceIcon.values: Free text or a symbolic code.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/VehicleArmourType.description: Armour type/item ID used by the vehicle. It is a reference.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/VehicleEnabled.description: If set, the vehicle is enabled in the game. It is a switch.

VEHICLES/VEHICLE/uiIndex.description: Index of the vehicle. It is an array key.
VEHICLES/VEHICLE/uiIndex.values: 0..255; the loader stores this field as UINT8.
